facts.fact: BetaToolRunner is an async iterable. Each iteration = exactly one API request; it yields the assistant BetaMessage (non-streaming) or BetaMessageStream (streaming) BEFORE any tools run, so you can inspect/intervene. After your loop body returns, the runner: reads stop_reason; appends the assistant message to params.messages; carries message.container.id forward; then determineNextStepFromStopReason: 'tool_use' -> run tools and push one user message of tool_result blocks, continue; 'pause_turn' or 'compaction' -> resume (re-send unchanged); 'end_turn' | 'stop_sequence' | 'max_tokens' | 'model_context_window_exceeded' | 'refusal' | null -> stop (unknown future values also stop). A `max_tokens` stop ends the loop with that message as final — the runner does not auto-retry; bump via setMessagesParams and continue yourself. The assistant/tool_result history is append-only (good for Opus 5.5 preserved-thinking checks).

The bundled doc warns the runner does not auto-resume `pause_turn` 'as of 0.110.0'. In the installed 0.133.0, determineNextStepFromStopReason returns 'resume' for 'pause_turn' and 'compaction', so the loop re-sends automatically (each resume still consumes a max_iterations tick). The doc's manual `runner.pushMessages({role:'assistant', content: message.content})` workaround is therefore unnecessary on 0.133.0 (and would duplicate the assistant turn, since the runner already appended it).

max_iterations counts API requests (sends), including resumes and compactions. Check happens at the top of each loop: `if (params.max_iterations && iterationCount >= params.max_iterations) break;` then `iterationCount++` before the send. When the cap is hit the loop ends even if the last message still requests tools (its tools are not executed, no tool_result is appended), and `done()` resolves with that last message — check its stop_reason ('tool_use' means the cap cut it off). Omit or 0/undefined = unlimited.

Each yielded BetaMessage has `.usage: BetaUsage` = { input_tokens: number; output_tokens: number; cache_creation_input_tokens: number | null; cache_read_input_tokens: number | null; cache_creation: { ephemeral_5m_input_tokens, ephemeral_1h_input_tokens } | null; output_tokens_details: { thinking_tokens } | null; iterations: BetaIterationsUsage | null (array of per-sampling-iteration entries with model/input/output/cache fields, incl. type 'fallback_message'); server_tool_use; service_tier: 'standard'|'priority'|'batch'|null; speed; inference_geo }. The runner does not aggregate — sum across iterations yourself. In streaming mode read it from `const m = await stream.finalMessage(); m.usage`. `runner.done()` returns only the final message (its own usage, not a total). input_tokens is the UNCACHED remainder; total prompt = input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens. Verified to type-check: `u.input_tokens + u.output_tokens + (u.cache_read_input_tokens ?? 0) + (u.cache_creation_input_tokens ?? 0)`.

Ways to stop: (a) `max_iterations`; (b) `break` out of `for await` — the iterator's finally aborts any in-flight stream and the pending tools for that message are not run (hold the message you already have; see unknowns re `done()` after break); (c) AbortSignal via `toolRunner(params, { signal })` or `runner.setRequestOptions({ signal })` -> request rejects with APIUserAbortError, and `ctx.signal` inside run() is aborted; (d) gate inside the tool's run() and return a 'declined' string; (e) take over with `runner.setMessagesParams(...)`/`pushMessages(...)` before tools execute (setMessagesParams marks the runner 'mutated', invalidates the cached tool response, and skips the automatic assistant-append for that turn). `runner.generateToolResponse(signal?)` lets you run/inspect the tool results yourself (cached, never runs a tool twice) and returns the tool_result user message or null.

`done(): Promise<BetaMessage>` waits for the iteration to complete (even if started elsewhere) and resolves with the final message; `runUntilDone(): Promise<BetaMessage>` consumes the whole iterator if not consumed, else waits; `await runner` == runUntilDone (then()). Throws AnthropicError('ToolRunner concluded without a message from the server') if nothing was processed and AnthropicError('Cannot iterate over a consumed stream') on a second iteration. `runner.params` is a readonly view of current params.

The runner adds NO `anthropic-beta` header by itself (only an X-Stainless helper header). Pass `betas: [...]` in params; messages.create turns `betas` into the `anthropic-beta` header (joined with commas). `addTools`/`removeTools` need beta `inline-tools-2026-09-15` and `compactBeforeNextTurn()` needs `compact-2026-09-04` — 'which the runner does not add for you'.

`stream: true` -> each iteration yields a BetaMessageStream (runner calls client.beta.messages.stream). Use `stream.on('text', delta => ...)`, `await stream.finalMessage()` (returns ParsedBetaMessage; rejects on error / premature end), `stream.finalText()`, `stream.currentMessage`, `stream.abort()`. A bare `message.stop_reason` check on the stream object never fires — resolve finalMessage() first. Optional `runToolsEagerly: true` (requires stream) starts each tool as soon as its tool_use block completes; use `runner.deferToolCall(block)` / `runner.deferredToolCalls` to hold unsafe calls. For streaming requests with user-defined tools, set `eager_input_streaming: true` on each tool (spread onto the betaZodTool), then rely on zod validation, check stop_reason max_tokens/refusal, and wrap the loop to catch the SDK's JSON parse error (rethrow Anthropic.APIError).

facts.topic: 5. Caching: the invariant and render order
facts.fact: Prompt caching is an exact prefix match: any byte change at position N invalidates every breakpoint at >= N. Render order is tools -> system -> messages, so a breakpoint on the last system block caches tools + system together. Max 4 `cache_control` breakpoints per request; allowed on system text blocks, tool definitions, and message content blocks (text, image, tool_use, tool_result, document). `cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }` = 5-minute TTL (write 1.25x); `{ type: 'ephemeral', ttl: '1h' }` = 1-hour (write 2x); reads refresh the timer; entries with the longer TTL must come before shorter ones. Minimum cacheable prefix on Opus 5.5 is 512 tokens (shorter silently doesn't cache: cache_creation_input_tokens 0). Caches are per workspace and model-scoped.

facts.topic: 5. Caching placement for system prompt + large transcript JSON + tools
facts.fact: Recommended layout for this project: (1) tools: a fixed, deterministically ordered list (sort by name), never changed mid-conversation (tools render at position 0; add/remove/reorder = full cache rebuild); (2) `system: [{ type: 'text', text: FROZEN_SYSTEM, cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' } }]` — one explicit breakpoint on the last static system block caches tools+system (no Date.now(), UUIDs, session IDs, conditional sections); (3) the large transcript JSON goes in the FIRST user message as its own text block with its own `cache_control` ('shared prefix, varying suffix' pattern) followed by the varying task text WITHOUT a marker — serialize it deterministically (stable key order; JSON.stringify of objects built in a fixed order, or sort keys) so the bytes are identical across runs; (4) plus top-level `cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }` on the request so the automatic breakpoint walks forward with the growing tool_use/tool_result tail (the 'robust combination for agent loops'; the automatic breakpoint consumes one of the 4 slots and must not have a different TTL than an explicit marker on the last block). This uses 3 of 4 breakpoints. Avoid putting the only marker after unique per-request content (pure write surcharge).

facts.topic: 5. Caching invalidation hierarchy relevant to this loop
facts.fact: Per the hierarchy table (Yes = that cache survives): tool definitions or model change -> everything invalidated; system prompt content change -> tools cache survives, system+messages invalidated; `tool_choice` or images -> tools+system survive, messages invalidated; `thinking`/`effort` change -> messages invalidated (tools/system model-specific) — pin effort per route; message content -> tools+system survive. On Opus 5.5 previous-turn thinking blocks are preserved, so a plain user message after tool use keeps the messages cache valid. Cache-preserving escape hatches: `{role:'system'}` message instead of editing top-level system (no beta on Opus 5.5); per-message effort (beta); `tool_addition`/`tool_removal` (beta mid-conversation-tool-changes-2026-07-01, runner addTools/removeTools under inline-tools-2026-09-15). 20-position lookback: a turn adding >20 positions (parallel tool_use runs collapse to one) can miss the previous entry — add an intermediate breakpoint ~every 15 positions. Parallel requests sharing a prefix all miss until the first response starts streaming.

Check `usage.cache_creation_input_tokens` (written, ~1.25x), `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` (read, 0.05x on Opus 5.5), `usage.input_tokens` (uncached remainder). Healthy loop signature: cache_read grows turn over turn; cache_creation is roughly the previous assistant output + newly appended input; input_tokens is just the tail after the last breakpoint. cache_read of zero across identical-prefix requests = silent invalidator (Date.now(), UUID, non-deterministic key order, varying tool set). `usage.cache_creation` splits writes by TTL (ephemeral_5m_input_tokens / ephemeral_1h_input_tokens). The SDK does not implement authentication itself. query() spawns the bundled Claude Code CLI as a subprocess and talks to it over stdio; the CLI resolves credentials from its environment and config dir.

Claude Code credential order: (1) cloud provider env (CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK/VERTEX/FOUNDRY), (2) ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, (3) ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, (4) apiKeyHelper, (5) CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from claude setup-token, (6) Anthropic profiles/federation, (7) subscription OAuth from /login, which the docs say is the default for Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise users. After /login, credentials are stored on Windows at %USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json (or under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR if that variable is set). The spawned CLI must be able to see that location.

If ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present, the CLI uses it in preference to a subscription login. The docs say that in non-interactive mode (-p) the key is always used when present, and that you should unset it to fall back to the subscription. design.title: Stage 3 planner — TOOL-USE-FIRST design (compact overview + exploration tools + strict submit_edl, validation loop inside the tool loop)
design.summary: The planner is a tool-use agent loop: the model receives a frozen system prompt plus ONE deterministic, cacheable "overview" block (video facts, preset, numbered phrase list with times, numbered shot/scene list, top highlights, silence gaps) and the user's instruction, and must explore with four read-only tools (get_transcript_range, get_scene_details, preview_frame → image block, validate_edl) before finishing with a strict submit_edl call. Validation and repair are NOT a separate harness re-prompt: submit_edl itself runs the full rule set (zod EdlSchema + range + word-cut + phrase/scene-boundary + duration + duplicates), auto-snaps edges ≤0.4 s, and returns either {accepted:true} or a machine-readable error list with suggested values; the model fixes and resubmits, up to 4 attempts. The harness only enforces outer limits (API iterations, rounds/nudges, preview budget, USD cap), stops the runner as soon as an EDL is accepted (runner.generateToolResponse() + break, saving the final round trip), and on exhaustion either fails the step cleanly (job.json 'failed', hints printed, pipeline resumable with `vedit plan`/`vedit cut --edl`) or, only with --allow-fallback, writes an honest `[fallback]` highlight-based EDL. Tools are defined once as backend-agnostic PlannerToolSpec objects (zod input schema + run → text/image) and adapted to three backends: `anthropic` (@anthropic-ai/sdk 0.133 client.beta.messages.toolRunner — the SPEC's "Claude API tool use", reference implementation, needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), `agent-sdk` (@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.296 query()+createSdkMcpServer, can run on the user's Claude Code subscription login — flagged as undocumented/policy-gray), and `mock` (scripted, for offline tests). Cost is computed per iteration from usage (per-model pricing table, cache fields, usage.iterations for fallbacks) and written as one cost.json entry per run plus a detailed plan.json report. Stage 5 (revise) reuses runPlanner() with mode:'revise' (task block carries the current EDL; same tools; same validation) and diffs outputs to re-cut only affected ids.

tools.name: get_transcript_range
tools.input: { "start"?: number (seconds), "end"?: number, "phrase_ids"?: number[], "words"?: boolean (default false) } — at least one selector (start+end, or phrase_ids). zod: z.object({ start: z.number().optional(), end: z.number().optional(), phrase_ids: z.array(z.number()).optional(), words: z.boolean().optional() }) with .describe() on every field; range/ids checked inside run (ToolError on start>=end, start>duration, unknown id, >50 ids).
tools.output: JSON text: { "range": [8.29, 23.10], "phrases": [{ "id": 3, "start": 8.29, "end": 11.02, "lang": "ru", "text": "Каждое утро мы ...", "words"?: [["Каждое", 8.29, 8.74], ...] }], "gaps": [[11.02, 11.60]], "truncated": false }. Phrases = transcript.segments overlapping the range (ids are segment indexes). If words=true and the span > 180 s, words are cut after 400 words and truncated=true with a note. Counter: maxTranscriptCalls (20); over limit → non-error text { "error": "transcript call budget exhausted; use the overview" }.
tools.why: The overview truncates phrase text to 80 chars and never includes word timings; this is how the model gets exact word boundaries and full text to pick clean in/out points and to write titles/captions language decisions.

tools.name: get_scene_details
tools.input: { "scene_ids"?: number[], "start"?: number, "end"?: number } — at least one selector; max 25 scenes per call. zod: z.object({ scene_ids: z.array(z.number()).optional(), start: z.number().optional(), end: z.number().optional() }).
tools.output: JSON text: { "scenes": [{ "id": 1, "start": 11.6, "end": 23.1, "duration": 11.5, "shot_type": "unknown", "people_count": 0, "emotion": "unknown", "objects": [], "quality_score": 0.5, "description": "[stub] shot 1, 11.5s, speech: ...", "is_stub": true, "frame": "shot_001.jpg" | null, "phrase_ids": [3, 4] }] }. is_stub = description starts with '[stub]'. frame = frames/shot_NNN.jpg if it exists for that index (documented assumption: scene index == shot index with the stub provider). Counter: maxSceneCalls (10).
tools.why: Gives the full scene record (the overview shows one line per scene) and the phrase↔scene overlap so the model can align clip edges to either boundary type as SPEC §5.3 requires.

tools.name: preview_frame
tools.input: { "timestamp": number (seconds, 0 ≤ t < duration), "note"?: string (why you look) }. zod: z.object({ timestamp: z.number(), note: z.string().optional() }). Out-of-range → ToolError with the valid range.
tools.output: Two content blocks: (1) text JSON { "timestamp": 12.4, "scene_id": 1, "phrase_id": 3 | null, "file": "frames/preview_012400.jpg", "previews_left": 9 } and (2) an image block { type: 'image', source: { type: 'base64', media_type: 'image/jpeg', data } } (agent-sdk: { type: 'image', data, mimeType: 'image/jpeg' } — verify). Frame extracted with extractFrame(media.normalized_path, t, <jobDir>/frames/preview_<ms padded 6>.jpg, 512) via injected deps; cached by ms key (re-asking the same ms does not consume budget); ffmpeg concurrency capped at 2 by a tiny semaphore in the session. Over budget (maxPreviewFrames=12) → non-error text { "error": "preview budget exhausted", "previews_left": 0 }. 512px-wide JPEG ≈ 200 input tokens.
tools.why: Vision is a stub today ('[stub]' descriptions carry no visual information); this is the only way the model can confirm what is on screen for a hook frame, a 9:16 crop, or a title moment — bounded so the cost stays predictable.

tools.name: validate_edl
tools.input: { "edl": EdlSubmit } where EdlSubmit = { "outputs": [{ "id": string, "aspect": "9:16"|"1:1"|"16:9", "target_duration"?: number, "clips": [{ "src_start": number, "src_end": number, "speed"?: number, "crop"?: "center"|"auto_face" }], "captions"?: { "enabled": boolean, "language"?: string, "style"?: string }, "titles"?: [{ "at": number, "duration"?: number, "text": string, "style"?: string }], "music"?: { "enabled": boolean }, "transitions"?: "cut" }], "reasoning": string }. The zod EdlSubmitSchema is strict-safe (no .default/.regex/.min/.max/.int); run() re-parses with the real EdlSchema (defaults, refinements, id regex) and reports those as E_SCHEMA.
tools.output: JSON text: { "ok": false, "errors": [{ "code": "E_WORD_CUT", "path": "outputs[0].clips[1].src_start", "message": "8.50 cuts the word \"Каждое\" (8.29–8.74); use 8.29", "suggested": 8.29 }], "warnings": [{ "code": "W_SOFT_BOUNDARY", "path": "...", "message": "..." }], "outputs": [{ "id": "reel_1", "clips": 3, "duration": 29.4, "target_duration": 30 }] }. Pure, no side effects, no auto-repair (so suggestions are explicit). Counter: maxValidateCalls (12).
tools.why: Lets the model check a draft cheaply before committing; identical rule set as submit_edl so there are no surprises, and it teaches the exact boundary times via `suggested`.

tools.name: submit_edl
tools.input: Same shape as validate_edl ({ "edl": EdlSubmit }). Marked strict: true on the anthropic backend (sanitized JSON schema, additionalProperties:false everywhere).
tools.output: Accepted: { "accepted": true, "attempt": 2, "repairs": ["outputs[0].clips[1].src_start 8.50→8.29 (word boundary)"], "warnings": [...], "outputs": [...], "next": "Done. Reply with one short sentence and do not call more tools." }. Rejected: { "accepted": false, "attempt": 1, "attempts_left": 3, "errors": [...same PlanIssue shape...], "warnings": [...], "hint": "Fix every error (use the suggested values) and call submit_edl again." }. Exhausted (attempt == maxSubmitAttempts, still invalid): { "accepted": false, "attempt": 4, "attempts_left": 0, "final": true, "errors": [...], "next": "Stop. The harness will use your best attempt." }. Side effects: records SubmitAttempt (with the repaired, parsed Edl when ok); sets session.accepted on success (a later valid submit in the same batch replaces it). Validation order inside run: EdlSubmitSchema parse (done by runner) → EdlSchema parse → autoRepair (snapClipsToWords ≤0.4 s, then snapToBoundaries ≤0.4 s) → validatePlan on the repaired EDL → accept iff errors.length === 0.
tools.why: The strict terminal tool is the contract: no free-text JSON parsing, the error feedback loop lives inside the tool protocol (one tool_result, no harness re-prompt), and acceptance is detected by the harness to stop the runner immediately.

design.prompt_outline:
REQUEST LAYOUT (anthropic backend; render order tools → system → messages; 3 of 4 cache breakpoints used):
1. tools: the five PlannerToolSpecs sorted by name, built once per run, never changed mid-conversation (tool order/content change = full cache rebuild). No cache_control on tools themselves.
2. system: [{ type:'text', text: SYSTEM_PROMPT, cache_control:{type:'ephemeral'} }] — one frozen constant string (PROMPT_VERSION bumps when edited). Contents, in order:
   a. Role: "You plan edits for an automated video editor. You never render; you produce an edit decision list (EDL) by calling tools."
   b. Inputs: "The first user message contains an OVERVIEW (video facts, preset, numbered PHRASES with start–end and truncated text, numbered SCENES, top HIGHLIGHTS, SILENCE GAPS) and then the TASK. Phrase ids = #n, scene ids = Sn. Full phrase text and word timings: get_transcript_range. Scene records and which phrases they contain: get_scene_details. What is actually on screen: preview_frame (descriptions prefixed [stub] carry NO visual information — do not invent people, emotions or objects)."
   c. Protocol: "Work by calling tools; several independent calls may go in one turn. Always call validate_edl at least once before submit_edl. You MUST finish by calling submit_edl and getting accepted:true. Fix every error it returns using the suggested values. After acceptance reply with one short sentence and stop. Do not restate the EDL in text. Do not describe your reasoning process in text; the EDL's `reasoning` field is a short editorial note for the user (2–5 sentences, in the user's language)." (Avoids reasoning_extraction declines.)
   d. Hard rules (verbatim, numbered): every clip edge is on a phrase boundary or a scene boundary (±0.15 s; use exact numbers from the overview/tools) — a cut inside a silence gap ≥0.5 s is tolerated with a warning; never cut inside a word; 0 ≤ src_start < src_end ≤ duration; clips ≥ preset min_clip_s; no duplicate clips; set target_duration per output and hit it within max(2 s, 10 %); ids filename-safe ([a-zA-Z0-9_-]), stable and meaningful (reel_1, wide_1); aspect from the deliverable (reels/shorts/stories → 9:16, YouTube/wide → 16:9, square posts → 1:1); captions.language is an ISO-639-1 code taken from the instruction (e.g. 'субтитры на узбекском' → 'uz'), captions.style = preset caption style; titles ≤ 6 words, title.at within the output's own timeline; speed ≠ 1 only on clips without speech; crop 'auto_face' for 9:16 when a person speaks on camera, else 'center'.
   e. Editorial guidance: hook = strongest phrase/visual in the first 2 s; one coherent story per output; prefer complete phrases; 'динамично/dynamic' = shorter clips and more cuts within preset pacing; keep chronology unless told otherwise; when N outputs are requested, minimise overlap between them and give each a distinct angle; respect the preset hints.
   f. Interpreting the instruction: derive N outputs, durations, platform/aspect, caption language, tone; when ambiguous pick sensible defaults and state the assumption in `reasoning`.
   g. Budgets (static numbers copied from DEFAULT_LIMITS): "at most 12 preview frames, 20 transcript calls, 10 scene calls, 12 validations, 4 submit attempts; plan your exploration."
   h. Revise mode: "If the TASK says REVISE, you receive the CURRENT EDL. Change only what the instruction asks, keep output ids stable, and leave untouched outputs byte-identical; mention what changed in `reasoning`."
3. messages[0] (user) content blocks: [ { type:'text', text: OVERVIEW (deterministic, from buildOverview), cache_control:{type:'ephemeral'} }, { type:'text', text: TASK block, no marker } ].
   OVERVIEW format (byte-stable, toFixed(2), fixed section order, no dates/ids):
   VIDEO: 35.00 s, 1920x1080 @30fps, audio: yes, language: ru (also: en) | PRESET bold_pop: <description>; captions style bold_pop (default on); titles style hero; pacing: clips 1.00–8.00 s; hints: ... | PHRASES (#id start–end [lang] text; full text/words via get_transcript_range): #0 0.52–3.10 [ru] Добро пожаловать в наше… | SCENES (Sid start–end type people quality — description): S0 0.00–11.60 unknown 0p q0.50 — [stub] shot 0, 11.6s, speech: "…" | HIGHLIGHTS (top 15, Hn start–end score — reason) | SILENCE GAPS ≥0.50 s: 3.10–3.80, … | NOTES: 'no speech detected' / 'vision is a stub' when applicable. Sizing for a 10-min video: ~200–250 phrases × ~45 tokens (Cyrillic) + ~100 scenes × 30 + highlights ≈ 15–18k tokens, all cached after the first request; phraseTextChars/maxScenes keep it bounded.
   TASK block: "TASK (plan)\nInstruction: <user prompt verbatim>\nProduce the EDL via tools; finish with submit_edl." — revise: "TASK (revise)\nInstruction: <text>\nCURRENT EDL:\n<stableStringify(currentEdl)>".
4. Top-level `cache_control: { type:'ephemeral' }` on the request so the automatic breakpoint walks forward with the growing tool_use/tool_result tail; same TTL as the explicit markers.
5. Other params: model, max_tokens 16000, output_config:{effort}, stream:false as const, max_iterations: remaining budget, tool_choice omitted (auto), betas/fallbacks only when VEDIT_PLAN_FALLBACKS=1 (betas:['server-side-fallback-2026-07-01'], fallbacks:'default').
Agent-sdk backend: systemPrompt = SYSTEM_PROMPT + "\nTool names are prefixed mcp__vedit__ (e.g. mcp__vedit__submit_edl)."; prompt = OVERVIEW + "\n\n" + TASK (caching handled by the CLI). Mock backend ignores prompts.
design.loop_and_validation:
LOOP (anthropic backend, src/plan/backends/anthropic.ts; policy decisions in src/plan/loop.ts so the mock backend reuses them):
```
state = { iterations:0, rounds:0, nudges:0, raisedMaxTokens:false, usd:0, accepted:false, submitExhausted:false, lastStop:null }
messages = [ seedUserMessage(overview, task) ]; maxTokens = limits.maxOutputTokens
while (true) {
  runner = client.beta.messages.toolRunner(buildParams(req, maxTokens, messages) /* object literal, stream:false as const, max_iterations: limits.maxIterations - state.iterations */)
  state.rounds++
  for await (const message of runner) {           // one API request per iteration; yielded BEFORE tools run
    state.iterations++; addUsage(message.usage); state.usd += usdForUsage(model, message.usage).usd; emit iteration
    if (message.stop_reason === 'refusal') { stop='refusal'; break }
    if (message.stop_reason === 'max_tokens') { stop='max_tokens'; break }     // truncated tool_use: never run it
    if (message.stop_reason === 'tool_use') {
      await runner.generateToolResponse()          // runs this message's tools NOW (cached; the runner will not run them twice)
      if (session.accepted) { stop='submitted'; break }   // skip the final confirmation round trip
      if (session.submitExhausted) { stop='attempts_exhausted'; break }
    }
    if (overBudget(state, limits)) { stop='budget'; break }
  }
  if (stop in ['submitted','attempts_exhausted','refusal','budget']) break
  // natural end: end_turn / stop_sequence / max_iterations (last message may still carry tool_use) / max_tokens
  messages = [...runner.params.messages]                          // runner appended assistant (+tool_result) messages (verify after a live run)
  const next = nextAction({ ...state, lastStop: last?.stop_reason ?? null, accepted: !!session.accepted, submitExhausted: session.submitExhausted }, limits)
  if (next.kind === 'nudge') { messages.push({ role:'user', content: NUDGE_MESSAGE }); state.nudges++; continue }   // append-only history keeps thinking signatures valid
  if (next.kind === 'retry_higher_max_tokens') { if (messages.at(-1)?.role === 'assistant') messages.pop(); maxTokens = limits.raisedOutputTokens; state.raisedMaxTokens = true; continue }
  stop = next.stop; break
}
```
nextAction rules: accepted → stop 'submitted'; iterations ≥ maxIterations or rounds ≥ maxRounds → 'max_iterations'; lastStop === 'max_tokens' && !raised → retry_higher_max_tokens (once; 20000 still ≤ 21333 non-streaming guard); lastStop === 'end_turn'|'stop_sequence' && nudges < maxNudges → nudge; else stop with the mapped reason. Never call runner.done() after a break (unknown: it may hang). Budget check uses the running USD total after each yielded message (no in-flight request at that moment, so a plain break suffices; AbortSignal also passed to tools via ctx.signal). Parallel tool_use blocks are executed by the runner and returned in one user message; preview_frame concurrency is limited inside the session. pause_turn/compaction are auto-resumed by the installed 0.133.0 runner (each resume costs one max_iterations tick). Errors: AuthenticationError → PlanError('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY отклонён/не задан — задайте в .env или используйте --backend agent-sdk'); BadRequestError whose message mentions strict/input_schema on the FIRST request → rebuild tools with strict=false and retry once (note recorded in plan.json: 'strict tools rejected by API, retried non-strict'); RateLimitError/InternalServerError after SDK retries (client maxRetries 3, timeout 600 s) and APIConnectionError (checked before APIError) → PlanError with the typed class name; everything accrued so far (usage/usd) is still logged to cost.json before rethrowing. Order of instanceof checks: AuthenticationError, BadRequestError, NotFoundError (bad model id/org access), RateLimitError, APIConnectionError, APIError.

TOOL-LEVEL LIMITS (PlanSession.record): per-tool counters (maxTranscriptCalls 20, maxSceneCalls 10, maxPreviewFrames 12, maxValidateCalls 12, maxSubmitAttempts 4) and maxToolCalls 60; exceeding a read tool's budget returns a normal text result telling the model to rely on the overview (not is_error, so it adapts rather than retries); invalid arguments throw ToolError (is_error:true) with the valid range; zod parse failures are converted by the runner to is_error results before run() is called. Each call is traced (tool, input, ok, ms, resultChars, image flag) into plan.json.

VALIDATION (src/plan/rules.ts validatePlan, same for validate_edl and submit_edl):
1. E_SCHEMA — EdlSchema.safeParse issues (paths via formatIssues style: 'outputs[0].clips[1].src_end: ...').
2. E_RANGE — src_start < 0, src_end > media.duration (+0.001 tolerance), src_end ≤ src_start. suggested = clamped value.
3. E_WORD_CUT — wordAt(words, edge, 0.03) hit (existing validate.ts); suggested = word.start for a start edge, word.end for an end edge.
4. E_BOUNDARY — distance from edge to nearest boundaryCandidate (phrase starts/ends ∪ scene starts/ends ∪ {0, duration}) > 0.15 s AND the edge is not inside a silence gap ≥0.5 s with no word within 0.25 s (that case is W_SOFT_BOUNDARY, a warning; opts.strictBoundaries=true turns it into E_BOUNDARY). suggested = nearest candidate that keeps the clip ≥ min_clip_s. If the transcript has no words at all, E_BOUNDARY becomes W_NO_SPEECH-level warning (scene boundaries only, sparse).
5. E_MIN_CLIP — (src_end − src_start)/speed < preset.pacing.min_clip_s (default 1.0). W_LONG_CLIP above max_clip_s.
6. E_DUPLICATE — identical (src_start, src_end) twice in one output; W_OVERLAP when two clips in one output overlap by > 50 % of the shorter one.
7. E_DURATION — target_duration set and |Σ(src_end−src_start)/speed − target| > max(2 s, 10 % of target); message includes actual vs target and the delta. W_TARGET_MISSING when absent.
8. E_TITLE_RANGE — title.at (+duration) beyond the output's expected duration; text empty is E_SCHEMA.
9. W_SPEED_ON_SPEECH — speed ≠ 1 on a clip that overlaps any word. W_NO_CAPTION_LANG — captions.enabled without language (cut/design will default to transcript.language).
Auto-repair (submit_edl only): autoRepair = snapClipsToWords(clips, transcript, 0.4) (existing) → snapToBoundaries(clips, ctx, 0.4) (nearest candidate not inside a word) → re-validate; repairs are returned to the model as strings. Accept iff no errors remain. The repaired Edl (post-EdlSchema parse, defaults filled) is what gets written.

ACCEPTANCE POLICY (plan()): stop 'submitted' → status 'ok' (or 'partial' if the accepted EDL carries warnings or the backend recorded notes such as the non-strict retry); otherwise bestAttempt() (fewest errors, latest) is NOT written as edl.json (an invalid EDL must never reach cut) → if opts.allowFallback: fallbackPlan() (greedy highlights by score, chronological, snapped to boundaries, reasoning '[fallback] planner stopped: <stop reason>; clips from highlights.json') → status 'partial'; else PlanError('планировщик не выдал валидный EDL (<stop>, <n> попыток, последние ошибки: …)', report) → runStep marks plan 'failed' and plan.json is still written with status 'failed' and the full trace/attempts for debugging. cost.json gets its entry in all three cases (finally block). edl.json is written with writeJson(EdlSchema) (atomic); plan.json with writeJson(PlanReportSchema). In `vedit run` the plan step runs inside runStep like the others; a PlanError is caught by the command's try/catch → fail() prints '✖ plan: …' plus hints ('повторить: vedit plan <id> -p "…"', 'или вручную: vedit cut <id> --edl <file>'); no stack trace, job stays resumable.

REVISE REUSE (stage 5): revise() loads the current edl.json, calls runPlanner(ctx, { mode:'revise', instruction, currentEdl }, backend, limits, deps) — identical tools, rules, loop; after acceptance diffEdl(before, after) → affected = added ∪ changed; backs up edl.json to edl.<n>.json, writes the new one and plan.json (mode:'revise'), then cut(jobId, edl, media, { only: affected, transcript, snap }) — note cut.json is rewritten whole by `--only` runs (existing behaviour; stage 5 should merge the previous cut.json entries for unaffected ids).
design.cost_and_caching:
USAGE → USD (src/plan/pricing.ts): for each yielded BetaMessage, if usage.iterations is present price each entry by its own `model` (covers server-side fallback rescues billed at the fallback model's rate), else price the top-level fields: usd = input_tokens·in + (cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens ?? cache_creation_input_tokens ?? 0)·cacheWrite5m + (cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens ?? 0)·cacheWrite1h + (cache_read_input_tokens ?? 0)·cacheRead + output_tokens·out, all /1e6; output_tokens already includes thinking (output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens is recorded separately for the report only); service_tier 'batch' → batch rates. PRICES['claude-opus-5-5'] = { in 4, out 20, cacheRead 0.2, cacheWrite5m 5, cacheWrite1h 8 } USD/MTok from the bundled docs — FLAG: confirm against the live pricing page before relying on the numbers; unknown model ids → usd 0 with units.unpriced = 1 and a warning in plan.json (never silently wrong). Agent-sdk backend: usd = result.total_cost_usd, per-model breakdown from result.modelUsage (inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens, costUSD), marked estimated:true; when the CLI ran on a subscription login this is an API-equivalent estimate, not billing — plan.json.cost_estimated=true and `vedit status` prints '≈'.

LOGGING: exactly one cost.json entry per planner run (also on failure, via finally): addCost(jobId, { step: 'plan' /* or 'revise' */, provider: 'anthropic' | 'claude-agent-sdk' | 'mock', model, units: { requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, thinking_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, tool_calls, preview_frames, submit_attempts, wall_seconds, estimated: 0|1, unpriced: 0|1 }, usd }). Local ffmpeg work for preview frames is not a separate entry (usd 0 convention) but is visible in units.preview_frames. plan.json additionally stores usage.per_iteration [{ i, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read, cache_write, stop_reason, tools, usd }] so cache health can be eyeballed: healthy = cache_read grows every iteration, input_tokens is only the new tail.

CACHING INVARIANTS (enforced by construction + tests): (1) tools array sorted by name, built once per run, same descriptions/schemas across runs (test: toolJsonSchema output is a snapshot); (2) SYSTEM_PROMPT is a constant — no Date.now, job ids, counts, or conditional sections (the budget numbers are compile-time constants); breakpoint on it caches tools+system (>512 tokens, so it does cache); (3) OVERVIEW is deterministic per job: buildOverview(ctx) twice === same string (test), stable key order, toFixed(2), sections in fixed order — breakpoint on it; identical across plan and revise runs of the same job so a revise within 5 min hits the cache, later runs pay a 1.25× rewrite (~$0.09 for 18k tokens) — acceptable, so the 5-minute TTL is used (no 1h TTL); (4) top-level cache_control walks the growing tail; (5) effort and model are pinned per run (changing them invalidates the messages cache); (6) nudges append a user message, never edit history, so Opus 5.5 thinking-block signatures stay valid; (7) strict-tool retry rebuilds the tools once → a full cache rebuild, accepted as a one-off and noted. Expected cost per 10-min video at effort medium: overview ~16k tokens written once ($0.08) then read ~15× ($0.05), tool results/tail ~20k tokens ($0.08 + cache), outputs ~15 × 1.5–2k tokens incl. thinking ($0.5–0.6), images 12 × ~200 tokens (negligible) → ≈ $0.7–0.9 per plan; the default maxUsd 3 cap stops runaway loops; `vedit plan --dry-run` prints the overview and, when an API key exists, client.beta.messages.countTokens({ model, system, tools, messages }) for a pre-flight input-token figure (no forced tool_choice, so countTokens is allowed).
design.offline_testing:
`npm test` stays `node --import tsx --test tests/*.test.ts`; tests/stage3.test.ts uses node:test + node:assert/strict, no ffmpeg, no network, no SDK calls (the SDK module is imported only by backends/anthropic.ts, which the tests never load except for the pure helpers that are exported from tools.ts/pricing.ts). Fixture: makeContext() builds a PlanContext inline (35 s video, 6 phrases ru/en with word timings, 3 scenes, 6 highlights, bold_pop preset) the way stage2.test.ts builds transcripts; a second fixture with 220 phrases/90 scenes generated programmatically checks sizing/determinism for the 10-min case.

Tests:
1. overview: buildOverview(ctx) === buildOverview(ctx); contains '#0 ', 'S0 ', 'HIGHLIGHTS'; phrase text truncated to phraseTextChars with '…'; 10-min fixture stays under a token proxy (chars/3 < 25k) and lists every phrase; overviewHash stable.
2. rules: E_WORD_CUT with suggested word.start/end; E_BOUNDARY off-boundary with suggested nearest candidate; silence-gap edge → W_SOFT_BOUNDARY (and E_BOUNDARY with strictBoundaries); E_RANGE for end > duration; E_DURATION outside max(2 s,10 %); E_DUPLICATE; E_TITLE_RANGE; valid EDL → ok with filled defaults; autoRepair snaps 0.3 s shifts and leaves 0.6 s shifts as errors; no-speech transcript downgrades boundary errors to warnings.
3. tools: get_transcript_range by range and by ids, words on/off, gaps, truncation at 180 s/400 words, ToolError on start>=end; get_scene_details frame null when file missing (deps.exists stub) and phrase_ids overlap; preview_frame with deps.extractFrame = async () => file and readFileBase64 = () => '/9j/…' returns text+image, caches same ms, returns budget-exhausted text after maxPreviewFrames; validate_edl pure (session.attempts unchanged); submit_edl reject → attempt recorded with errors, accept → session.accepted is the repaired Edl, exhausted → final:true.
4. schemas: for every tool, toolJsonSchema(spec) has type:'object', additionalProperties:false on all nested objects, and contains none of $schema/default/pattern/minimum/maximum/minLength/maxLength; EdlSubmitSchema accepts the SPEC §5.3 example and rejects additional keys; the real EdlSchema still rejects a bad id via E_SCHEMA.
5. loop policy: nextAction table — accepted→submitted; end_turn with nudges<2→nudge, with nudges=2→end_turn; max_tokens first→retry_higher_max_tokens, second→max_tokens; iterations cap→max_iterations; overBudget boundary.
6. pricing: usdForUsage('claude-opus-5-5', { input 1000, output 500, cache_read 10000, cache_creation 2000 (5m) }) === (4000+10000+2000+10000)/1e6 → 0.026 (check arithmetic in test); iterations array with a fallback entry priced by its own model; unknown model → unpriced.
7. mock backend end-to-end: process.env.VEDIT_WORKSPACE = mkdtemp BEFORE `await import('../src/plan/index.ts')` (WORKSPACE_ROOT is computed at module load); write media.json/transcript.json/scenes.json/highlights.json/job.json/cost.json into <tmp>/<jobId>; script = [{calls:[get_transcript_range]}, {calls:[validate_edl bad]}, {calls:[submit_edl bad]}, {calls:[submit_edl good]}] → plan() resolves status 'ok', edl.json exists and parses, plan.json has attempts [reject, accept], trace length 4, stop_reason 'submitted', cost.json has one 'plan' entry with provider 'mock', usd 0, units.tool_calls 4.
8. exhaustion: script submits bad 4× → plan() rejects with PlanError, plan.json status 'failed' written, no edl.json; same script with allowFallback:true → edl.json with reasoning starting '[fallback]' and status 'partial'.
9. never-submits: script = [{text:'done'}] → MockBackend applies nextAction → 2 nudges recorded, then stop 'end_turn' → PlanError; assert report.nudges === 2.
10. revise hooks: diffEdl(before, after) reports changed/added/removed/unchanged ids; buildTaskBlock({mode:'revise'}) embeds stableStringify(currentEdl) deterministically.
MockBackend contract: executes spec.run for each scripted call through session.record (so counters/trace are real), feeds ToolOutput history to function-style scripts (adaptive mocks can read submit_edl's errors and 'fix' them), emits fake IterationUsage (zeros by default), and returns BackendResult with the same StopReason semantics as the anthropic backend. Injectable deps (PlanDeps) avoid ffmpeg; AnthropicBackend also accepts an injected `client` so a future test can feed canned BetaMessages through a stub toolRunner, but that is optional. Live verification is manual: tests/plan-live.ts on job 20261010-7d76cd prints per-iteration usage and asserts cache_read_input_tokens > 0 from iteration 2, strict acceptance, and that an image tool result was accepted. Prerequisite: fix the pre-existing tests/make-fixtures.ts type errors so `npm run typecheck` is green before stage-3 code lands.
design.cli:
Shared planner options via addPlannerOptions(cmd) (Russian help text like the rest of cli.ts): `--backend <auto|anthropic|agent-sdk|mock>` (default auto), `--model <id>` (default claude-opus-5-5; env VEDIT_PLAN_MODEL), `--effort <low|medium|high|xhigh|max>` (default medium; env VEDIT_PLAN_EFFORT), `--max-usd <n>` (default 3), `--max-iterations <n>` (default 24), `--allow-fallback` (write a [fallback] EDL from highlights if the agent fails), `--strict-tools/--no-strict-tools` (default strict).

`vedit run <video> -p "3 рилса по 30 секунд для кафе, динамично, субтитры на узбекском" --preset bold_pop [planner options]`: after ingest and understand, branch: `--edl` given → unchanged behaviour (stageEdl, skip the agent); else `--prompt` given → `console.log('▸ plan')`; `const r = await runStep(job.id, 'plan', () => plan(job.id, media, { prompt, preset, backend, model, effort, limits, allowFallback, onEvent }))`; printPlanReport(r); then cut as today with r.edl. Neither → the current informational message, reworded to mention `vedit plan <id> -p "…"`. --skip-understand with --prompt → plan still runs (no transcript → scene boundaries only; warning printed). onEvent prints live progress: `  ↳ get_transcript_range {start:8.29,end:23.1}` (one line per tool call, 2-space + arrow), `  ↳ submit_edl ✖ 2 ошибки` / `✔ принят (попытка 2)`. printPlanReport prints: `  backend: anthropic claude-opus-5-5 effort=medium` (plus the backend note when not the API key), `  инструменты: get_transcript_range×4, get_scene_details×1, preview_frame×2, validate_edl×1, submit_edl×2`, per output `  ✔ reel_1: 9:16, 3 клипа, 29.40s (цель 30s), субтитры uz` and `    ⚠ <warning>` lines, `  reasoning: <first 200 chars>`, `  $0.41 (12 запросов, 38k in / 6k out, cache hit 91%)` or `≈$0.41` when estimated. Plan failure → caught by the command's try/catch → fail('plan: <message>\n  повторить: vedit plan <id> -p "…"\n  или вручную: vedit cut <id> --edl <file>') — job.json keeps steps.plan 'failed', plan.json has the trace.

`vedit plan <job_id> -p/--prompt <text> [--preset <name>] [planner options] [--dry-run]`: re-plans an existing job: loadJob, media.json required, transcript/scenes/highlights optional (warnings); stores prompt/preset into job.json (writeJson JobSchema) so `vedit status` shows them; `--dry-run` prints the overview, its hash, the resolved backend note, and the countTokens figure when an API key exists, without calling the model; otherwise runStep('plan', …) + printPlanReport. Does not cut (run `vedit cut <id>` afterwards; the command prints that hint).

`vedit revise <job_id> -p <text> [planner options] [--no-cut]`: stage 5 — calls revise() (same options), prints the diff (`  ~ reel_1: clips, titles` / `  + reel_3` / `  - wide_1` / `  = reel_2`), then cut with `only: affected` unless --no-cut. Until stage 5 lands the action stays fail('revise появится на этапе 5') but the option group is already attached.

`vedit status <job_id>`: after the understand line, if plan.json exists print `план: <backend> <model>, <status>, попыток <n>, вызовов <tool_calls>, превью <preview_frames>, $<cost_usd>[≈]` and the first line of error when failed; `стоимость API:` line stays (now non-zero).

Env/config: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN) from .env via existing process.loadEnvFile(); VEDIT_PLAN_BACKEND / VEDIT_PLAN_MODEL / VEDIT_PLAN_EFFORT / VEDIT_PLAN_MAX_USD as defaults for the options; VEDIT_PLAN_FALLBACKS=1 enables server-side fallbacks on the anthropic backend. .env.example gains the VEDIT_PLAN_* lines and a comment that without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY the agent-sdk backend uses the Claude Code login. README status table: stage 3 → 'tool-use planner (anthropic | agent-sdk | mock)'. Also bump program.version to match package.json (0.3.0).
risks: Subscription login through the Agent SDK is undocumented and the SDK docs state third-party products may not offer claude.ai login; for this personal tool it is the only key-less path. Keep `anthropic` as the reference backend, surface the backend note in plan.json/status, and let the user decide; verify with one live run that the spawned claude.exe actually picks up %USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json (not observed in research).

strict: true on betaZodTool tools is unverified against the live API with zod 4's raw schema ($schema key, optional properties, `default`/`pattern` from .default()/.regex()). Mitigation in design: a strict-safe EdlSubmitSchema, sanitizeToolSchema (strips $schema/default/pattern/bounds, forces additionalProperties:false), a unit test on the emitted schema, and a one-shot non-strict retry on BadRequestError. Also unverified whether the API tolerates `$schema` in NON-strict mode (sanitizer removes it anyway).

Forced tool_choice is not available on claude-opus-5-5, so the model may end its turn without submitting; handled by up to 2 append-only nudges and clear prompt wording, but a run can still finish as 'end_turn' → failed step (resumable, cost logged).

runner.params.messages must contain the appended assistant/tool_result messages after a natural loop end for nudge/max_tokens continuation to work; generateToolResponse()+break must not re-run tools. Both read from BetaToolRunner.js in the research but not exercised live — tests/plan-live.ts must confirm; never await runner.done() after a break (may hang).

Agent SDK unknowns: image content blocks in MCP tool results reaching the model (preview_frame degrades to text-only with a 'frame saved at <path>' note if not), the exact `effort`/thinking option names, whether tools: [] also removes ToolSearch/Agent/TodoWrite (check the init message's tools array, logged to plan.json), Windows behaviour with the Cyrillic cwd (set cwd to the job dir and consider CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME), and that total_cost_usd/modelUsage are estimates.

Pricing table values ($4/$20, cache $0.2/$5/$8 per MTok) come from bundled docs dated before today; confirm on the live pricing page. Unknown models log usd 0 with units.unpriced=1 rather than guessing. Agent-sdk costs on a subscription are API-equivalent estimates (flagged estimated:true) and inflate total_usd relative to real spend.

Overview size for long videos (10 min ≈ 15–18k tokens) is cached but a 5-minute TTL means a later revise pays a 1.25× rewrite; any non-determinism (key order, toFixed drift, preset text edits) silently kills cache hits — the determinism test and per-iteration cache_read logging are the guard. The 20-position cache lookback can miss if one turn adds >20 blocks (many parallel tool calls); keep maxToolCalls per turn effectively bounded by the per-tool budgets.

Vision is a stub: scene descriptions carry no visual information, so clip choice is transcript-driven; preview_frame (12 max) is the only visual signal, and auto_face crop still falls back to center in cut. Scene index == shot index for frame lookup is an assumption that breaks once a real vision provider returns merged scenes (frameForScene returns null then; ScenesSchema should later gain a frame field).

Boundary rule interpretation: SPEC says phrase OR scene boundary; this design tolerates cuts inside silence gaps ≥0.5 s as warnings (W_SOFT_BOUNDARY) because they are editorially valid — switchable to strict via opts.strictBoundaries. Scene boundaries from ffmpeg scene>0.3 at 320px may be sparse, so no-speech videos may have few legal cut points; the model is told so in the overview.

Thinking tokens are billed as output and count toward max_tokens; at effort high/xhigh a 16k max_tokens may truncate (handled by one retry at 20k, still under the 21333 non-streaming SDK guard); switching to streaming later requires eager_input_streaming handling and is out of scope.

Asking for `reasoning` text could, if phrased badly, invite reasoning_extraction declines on Opus 5.5; the prompt frames it as a short editorial note for the user, never a reproduction of the model's reasoning. stop_reason 'refusal' is handled (no tools run, step fails with the category from stop_details).

Operational: the pre-existing typecheck failure in tests/make-fixtures.ts must be fixed first; cut.json is overwritten by --only runs (affects stage-5 bookkeeping); cost.json/edl.json writes are atomic via writeJson but plan.json + edl.json + cost.json are three separate writes (a crash between them leaves a consistent-but-partial job; `vedit status` shows it).

design.title: Stage 3 planner — CONTEXT-FIRST / FEWEST CALLS design (structured-output EDL by phrase/scene ids, harness-side validation, repair-on-failure)
design.summary: The planner is a single structured-output call. The harness builds one deterministic, cached "context pack" (media summary, every transcript phrase with an id p0..pN and its text/lang/times, every scene with an id s0..sM, the ranked highlights mapped to phrase ids, the preset) and asks claude-opus-5-5 (adaptive thinking, effort explicitly "medium") for a PlanDraft via output_config.format = betaZodOutputFormat(PlanDraftSchema). The draft never contains seconds: each clip is {start: "<ref>", end: "<ref>"} where a ref is a phrase/scene id ("p12", "s3", optionally "p12.end"/"s3.start"). The harness resolves refs to times (so SPEC's "every clip starts/ends on a phrase or scene boundary" holds by construction), snaps scene edges that land inside a word with the existing snapClipsToWords (<=0.4 s), runs all other checks (unknown ids, empty clips, media bounds, duration vs target, output count vs the model's own self-reported brief, filename-safe unique ids, titles inside the timeline), and writes edl.json. Only if errors remain does it append the issue list to the SAME conversation (append-only; thinking blocks preserved) and ask for a corrected full plan, at most 2 repairs. Happy path = 1 API call; with a repair or a frame preview = 2. The four SPEC tools (get_transcript_range, get_scene_details, preview_frame, validate_edl) are declared on every request (fixed, name-sorted, so the tools+system prefix caches) but the system prompt tells the model they are optional and when each is worth a round-trip; in FULL mode (<= ~40k pack tokens, which covers every video up to 10 min) the transcript/scene tools are redundant by design. Backends are pluggable behind PlannerBackend {start, continue}: AnthropicApiBackend (@anthropic-ai/sdk beta toolRunner + structured output + prompt caching + exact per-call usage pricing — the SPEC "Claude API (tool use)" path, needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), AgentSdkBackend (@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk query() with an in-process MCP server exposing the same tools and outputFormat json_schema — the only path that can use the user's Claude Code subscription login today; cost = SDK's client-side estimate), and MockBackend (scripted turns that still execute the real tool code; drives all offline tests). Stage 5 revise reuses everything: same pack (same cached bytes), the current EDL is reverse-mapped to a draft with ids (draftFromEdl), one call returns the full new draft, the harness validates/repairs the same way, diffs old vs new outputs, and cut() is re-run only for added/changed ids. Cost is logged to cost.json per API call (provider/model/units/usd) via the existing addCost, and plan.json records calls, repairs, tool calls, issues, usage and USD. Every failure path (API error, refusal, max_tokens, exhausted repairs) leaves job.json step 'plan' = failed/partial with the draft on disk, costs logged, and the job reusable via vedit plan / vedit cut --edl.
design.backend_choice:
DECISION: implement a small backend interface and ship two real backends plus a mock; default selection is automatic.

PlannerBackend (src/plan/backend/types.ts):
  interface PlannerBackend {
    readonly name: 'api' | 'agent' | 'mock';
    readonly model: string;
    start(req: StartRequest): Promise<Turn>;                       // first call: system + pack + task (+ tools)
    continue(prev: Turn, userText: string): Promise<Turn>;         // repair / follow-up in the same conversation
  }
  interface StartRequest { system: string; packText: string; taskText: string; tools: PlannerTool[]; outputSchema: z.ZodType; maxTokens: number; signal?: AbortSignal }
  interface Turn { text: string | null; stopReason: 'end_turn'|'max_tokens'|'refusal'|'max_iterations'|'error'; refusalCategory?: string; toolCalls: ToolCallRecord[]; usage: NormalizedUsage; usd: number; priced: boolean; calls: number; handle: unknown /* backend-private continuation state */ }
  interface NormalizedUsage { input_tokens: number; output_tokens: number; cache_read_input_tokens: number; cache_creation_input_tokens: number }
  interface ToolCallRecord { name: string; input: unknown; ok: boolean; ms: number; summary: string }

1) AnthropicApiBackend (src/plan/backend/anthropic.ts) — PRIMARY, the SPEC §4 "Claude API (tool use)" path. Uses only APIs from the research notes:
  - new Anthropic({ maxRetries: 3, timeout: 600_000 }) — explicit timeout so the SDK's non-streaming max_tokens>21333 guard never throws when we bump max_tokens on retry; retries 429/5xx/529/connection errors itself.
  - Session objects built ONCE per backend instance and reused for every request (cache stability): systemBlocks = [{type:'text', text: SYSTEM_PROMPT, cache_control:{type:'ephemeral'}}], apiTools = tools.map(t => { const tool = betaZodTool({ name, description, inputSchema: z.object(t.inputShape), run: adapt(t.run) }); delete (tool.input_schema as any).$schema; return tool; }) sorted by name. No strict:true (research unknown: raw zod keys $schema/minimum under strict). The $schema delete is defensive; verify once live whether the API tolerates it instead.
  - start(): runner = client.beta.messages.toolRunner({ model, max_tokens, max_iterations: 8, stream: false as const, output_config: { effort, format: betaZodOutputFormat(outputSchema) }, cache_control: { type:'ephemeral' }, system: systemBlocks, tools: apiTools, messages: [{ role:'user', content: [ { type:'text', text: packText, cache_control:{type:'ephemeral'} }, { type:'text', text: taskText } ] }] } satisfies BetaToolRunnerParams). `thinking` omitted (= adaptive on Opus 5.5). No tool_choice (auto; forced choice is a 400 on Opus 5.5). No fallbacks by default (a rescue would run on another model without thinking and at other prices; expose VEDIT_FALLBACKS=1 to add betas:['server-side-fallback-2026-07-01'], fallbacks:'default').
  - Iterate `for await (const message of runner)`: per message accumulate usage (input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens ?? 0, cache_creation_input_tokens ?? 0; usd via pricing.usdForUsage(model, message.usage) which prices usage.iterations[] per model when present), record tool_use blocks as ToolCallRecords (results come from the tool run() wrappers via onCall), remember `last = message`. Never `break` (research unknown: done() after break may hang). After the loop: stopReason = last.stop_reason mapped ('tool_use' at loop end ⇒ 'max_iterations'); text = last.content.filter(b => b.type==='text').map(b => b.text).join(''); handle = { messages: [...runner.params.messages] } (runner appends every assistant message and tool_result user message itself, so this is the full append-only transcript incl. thinking blocks).
  - 'refusal' ⇒ Turn.stopReason='refusal', refusalCategory = last.stop_details?.category. 'max_tokens' ⇒ backend retries ONCE with max_tokens 32000 on a fresh runner built from the request messages (the truncated assistant message is not replayed), then returns whatever it gets.
  - continue(prev, userText): same runner construction with messages: [...prev.handle.messages, { role:'user', content: userText }] — identical system/tools/effort/model objects ⇒ tools+system+pack are cache hits; only the tail is new. Append-only, so Opus 5.5 preserved-thinking binding is never violated.
  - Error mapping (typed classes, most specific first, never string-match): Anthropic.AuthenticationError ⇒ PlanError('ANTHROPIC_API_KEY отклонён — проверьте ключ или используйте --backend agent'); NotFoundError ⇒ model id / not enabled; RateLimitError (after SDK retries) ⇒ 'лимит API, повторите позже'; APIConnectionError (check before APIError) ⇒ network; BadRequestError ⇒ message + request id; APIError ⇒ generic. On the FIRST request only: if BadRequestError and tools were declared, retry once with tools omitted and record warning 'api_rejected_tools_with_format' (feature detection for the unverified output_config.format + client-tools combination); if that also fails, throw.
  - format.parse(text) is called by the loop, not the backend (the loop owns validation); the backend only returns raw text.

2) AgentSdkBackend (src/plan/backend/agent.ts) — FALLBACK for the user's current situation (no API key, Claude Code subscription login). Verified in the installed sdk.d.ts this session: Options has model, systemPrompt (string), effort: EffortLevel, thinking: {type:'adaptive'}, outputFormat: { type:'json_schema', schema }, maxTurns, maxBudgetUsd, mcpServers, tools, allowedTools, permissionMode, settingSources, resume: string, cwd; SDKResultSuccess has result, total_cost_usd, modelUsage, structured_output?: unknown; error subtypes include error_max_structured_output_retries.
  - server = createSdkMcpServer({ name:'vedit', version:'1.0.0', tools: tools.map(t => tool(t.name, t.description, t.inputShape, async (args) => toMcpResult(await t.run(args)))) }) where toMcpResult maps ToolResult to { content:[{type:'text',text}, ...images.map(i => ({type:'image', data:i.base64, mimeType:'image/jpeg'}))], isError }. ImageContent exists in the installed @modelcontextprotocol/sdk types; verify live that the CLI forwards it to the model as an image.
  - start(): for await (m of query({ prompt: packText + '\n\n' + taskText, options: { systemPrompt: SYSTEM_PROMPT, model, effort, thinking:{type:'adaptive'}, outputFormat: { type:'json_schema', schema: stripSchemaKey(z.toJSONSchema(outputSchema)) }, mcpServers:{ vedit: server }, tools: [], allowedTools: ['mcp__vedit__*'], permissionMode:'dontAsk', settingSources: [], maxTurns: 12, maxBudgetUsd: 3, cwd: jobDir } })). Keep the 'system' init message (check its tools array contains only mcp__vedit__* — log otherwise) and capture session_id for continuation. On result: text = JSON.stringify(m.structured_output) when present, else m.result; usage from m.modelUsage (sum over models: inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens); usd = m.total_cost_usd, priced=false (SDK estimate, not billing). Error subtypes ⇒ Turn.stopReason='error' with the message; error_max_turns ⇒ 'max_iterations'. Wrap the loop in try/catch (query() throws after an error result in single-prompt mode).
  - continue(): query({ prompt: userText, options: { ...same, resume: prev.handle.sessionId } }). Verify live that `resume` replays the MCP tools + outputFormat exactly; fallback if it does not: stateless repair (new query with pack + previous draft JSON + issues).
  - env: do NOT pass options.env (it replaces, not merges, the subprocess env; the CLI needs USERPROFILE to find %USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json). If ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set the CLI would use it, but then the api backend was auto-selected anyway.
  - Policy note printed once when this backend is selected: subscription login via the Agent SDK is undocumented for third-party products per Anthropic docs ("Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login..."); personal, non-distributed use is not addressed — the user should confirm against the Commercial Terms; this is not legal advice. The api backend is the supported path.

3) MockBackend (src/plan/backend/mock.ts) — tests only. new MockBackend({ model?: 'mock', turns: MockTurn[] }) where MockTurn = { tools?: Array<{ name: string; input: unknown }>; text: string | object; stopReason?: Turn['stopReason']; usage?: Partial<NormalizedUsage> }. start/continue pop the next turn, execute each listed tool by calling the REAL PlannerTool.run from req.tools (so tool code is covered offline), store the tool results in handle for assertions, and return text (object ⇒ JSON.stringify). Records every userText it received (mock.received: string[]) so tests can assert the repair message carried the issue codes.

Selection (src/plan/backend/index.ts): selectBackend(choice: 'auto'|'api'|'agent'|'mock', env = process.env, deps): { backend: PlannerBackend; note: string }. 'auto' ⇒ 'api' if env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN) is set, else 'agent' if the win32-x64 claude.exe optional dependency resolves (require.resolve('@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-win32-x64/claude.exe') in try/catch) — note 'backend: agent (подписка Claude Code; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY не задан)', else PlanError('нет ANTHROPIC_API_KEY и не найден Claude Code CLI — задайте ключ в .env или выполните claude login'). 'mock' only via PlanOptions.backendInstance (tests) or VEDIT_PLANNER=mock with a fixture file path (manual demos). The note is printed by the CLI and stored in plan.json.backend_note.

Model/effort: default model 'claude-opus-5-5' (research: current Opus, 1M context, $4/$20, structured outputs supported); effort explicitly 'medium' for plan, repair AND revise (pinned per conversation — changing it mid-conversation invalidates the messages cache), overridable with --effort. max_tokens 16000 (docs default; well under the 21333 non-streaming guard), bumped to 32000 on a max_tokens stop. Non-streaming is used because output is a few KB of JSON; the explicit client timeout makes that safe.

files.purpose: Zod contracts for the planner: the model-facing draft (ids, not seconds), issues, plan.json and revise.json reports. All schemas use plain z.number()/z.string() with NO .min/.max/.regex so the JSON schema sent as output_config.format is clean; constraints live in resolve.ts. Optional fields use .optional() (verify once live that non-required properties are accepted; fallback .nullable()).

Minimal style-preset contract so --preset bold_pop resolves to something the prompt can use (presets/ is currently empty). Add `export * from './preset.ts'` and `export * from './plan.ts'` to src/schemas/index.ts.

export const PresetSchema = z.object({ name: z.string(), description: z.string(), pace: z.enum(['dynamic','calm','neutral']), clip_seconds: z.object({ min: z.number(), max: z.number() }), caption_style: z.string(), title_style: z.string().default('hero'), default_aspect: AspectSchema.default('9:16'), music_default: z.boolean().default(false), notes: z.array(z.string()).default([]) });
export type Preset = z.infer<typeof PresetSchema>;
