tools.name: get_transcript_range
tools.input: { "start": number /* seconds, clamped to [0, media.duration] */, "end": number /* > start; end-start <= 180 else is_error 'range too long' */ }
tools.output: text (JSON): { "phrases": [ { "id": "p4", "start": 12.40, "end": 17.90, "lang": "ru", "text": "...full text...", "words": [ { "w": "Каждое", "start": 8.29, "end": 8.74 }, ... ] } ] } — every phrase overlapping [start,end]; [] when there is no speech there.
tools.why: Redundant in FULL mode (the whole transcript with ids is already in the pack), so the system prompt says not to call it then. Exists for (a) COMPACT mode (videos whose pack exceeds ~40k tokens: phrase texts are truncated to 60 chars and the model must fetch full text for candidate ranges) and (b) word-level timing when the model wants to judge a scene-boundary cut next to speech. Cheap (text only); each call is one extra API round-trip, so the prompt asks for all needed ranges in one turn (parallel tool_use).

tools.name: get_scene_details
tools.input: { "id": "s3" }  (scene id; unknown id => is_error 'unknown scene id s9; valid: s0..s2')
tools.output: text (JSON): { "id": "s3", "start": 23.10, "end": 35.00, "description": "[stub] shot 2, 11.9s, speech: ...", "objects": [], "people_count": 0, "emotion": "unknown", "shot_type": "unknown", "quality_score": 0.5, "phrases": [ { "id": "p6", "start": 24.1, "end": 28.0, "text": "..." } ], "edges": { "start": { "inside_word": { "w": "Каждое", "start": 8.29, "end": 8.74 } | null, "safe_start": 8.29 }, "end": { "inside_word": null, "safe_end": 35.0 } }, "prev": "s2" | null, "next": null }
tools.why: In FULL mode everything except `edges` is already in the pack; `edges` tells the model whether cutting on this scene boundary would cut a word and what the harness will snap it to — useful only when the model deliberately plans a scene-boundary cut inside speech. Primary use is COMPACT mode (truncated descriptions).

tools.name: preview_frame
tools.input: { "t": number /* seconds in [0, media.duration]; otherwise is_error */ }
tools.output: content blocks: [ { type: 'image', JPEG 640px wide extracted at t from media.normalized_path (cached at <jobDir>/frames/preview_<t_ms>.jpg) }, { type: 'text', text: 'frame at 12.400s — scene s1 (11.60–23.10), phrase p4 "..."; frames used 2/6' } ]. Budget exhausted => is_error 'frame budget 6/6 used — decide from the scene list'. Implemented with extractFrame() from src/understand/shots.ts (injectable in tests).
tools.why: The only source of visual truth: with the stub vision provider every scene description is '[stub] ...' and carries no visual information (people_count 0, emotion unknown), and the honest-stub convention forbids the model from inventing visuals. The system prompt restricts it to instructions that depend on what is visible ('начни с фасада', 'покажи блюда', speaker must be in frame for 9:16) and tells the model to request all candidate frames (scene midpoints) in ONE turn so the whole visual check costs one extra API call (~300 input tokens per 640x360 image). Also the natural hook for a future real vision provider: when descriptions are not [stub] the prompt says frames are rarely needed.

tools.name: validate_edl
tools.input: { "plan": PlanDraft } — exactly the structured-output schema (ids, not seconds). betaZodTool parses it with PlanDraftSchema before run(); malformed input => is_error with the zod issues.
tools.output: text (JSON): { "ok": boolean, "errors": PlanIssue[], "warnings": PlanIssue[], "resolved": [ { "id": "reel_1", "duration_s": 29.4, "target_s": 30, "clips": [ { "start_s": 12.40, "end_s": 17.90, "from": "p4", "to": "p5" } ] } ] } — produced by the same resolveDraft() the harness runs on the final answer (one implementation, so the tool can never disagree with the harness).
tools.why: Required by SPEC §5.3 and genuinely useful for self-correction, but in the fewest-calls design it is NOT needed on the happy path: the harness validates the final answer for free and sends issues back only when there are errors, which costs the same one round-trip a tool call would. The prompt therefore says: do not call it routinely; call it when the plan is unusual (more than 3 outputs, more than 15 clips, deliberate scene/phrase boundary mixing, or after preview_frame changed the plan) and you prefer to fix issues before answering. In revise it is slightly more valuable because the model edits an existing plan with t-refs it must not break.

design.prompt_outline:
Request layout (API backend), in cache-render order tools -> system -> messages, 3 of 4 breakpoints used:
  [tools]   4 tools, name-sorted, same object instances for every request of the job (never reordered/added/removed).
  [system]  one text block = SYSTEM_PROMPT (frozen, English, no job data, no dates) + cache_control ephemeral (ttl per cacheTtl). Caches tools+system across all jobs on the machine for 5 min / 1 h.
  [messages[0].content[0]] = pack text, cache_control ephemeral — job-static, byte-identical for every call of this job (plan, repairs, revise).
  [messages[0].content[1]] = task text, no marker — varies (instruction / revise edit).
  [top-level cache_control ephemeral] — automatic breakpoint that walks forward over the tool_use/tool_result/repair tail.
Agent backend: systemPrompt = SYSTEM_PROMPT; prompt = pack + '\n\n' + task (caching handled by the CLI).

SYSTEM_PROMPT sections (in order):
 1. Role. "You are the planning stage of an automated video editor. You receive an analysis pack for one source video and an editing instruction (usually Russian or Uzbek). You produce a cut plan as JSON. You never render video."
 2. The pack format: keys media {duration_s, fps, w, h, has_audio, language, languages, mode}, phrases [{id,start,end,lang,text}] (in FULL mode text is complete; in COMPACT mode text is truncated to 60 chars and you must use get_transcript_range), scenes [{id,start,end,shot_type,people,emotion,q,description,phrases}], highlights [{rank,score,start,end,phrases,reason}] (ranked best first; the ranking uses only measurable signals), preset {name, pace, clip_seconds, caption_style, title_style, default_aspect, notes}.
 3. Honesty rules. "Descriptions starting with [stub] contain NO visual information: do not claim what is shown, do not refer to people/emotions that the pack does not state; the only way to learn what is visible is preview_frame. Never quote text that is not in a phrase. Highlight reasons are heuristics, not facts."
 4. Hard rules for the plan (each clip edge is a ref; the harness turns refs into times):
    - A ref is a phrase id (p12) or scene id (s3), optionally with .start/.end. In `start` the default edge is .start, in `end` it is .end: {start:"p3", end:"p5"} means from the start of p3 to the end of p5. Never write seconds. (Revise mode: refs of the form t12.400 may appear in the current plan for clips that were hand-edited; keep them verbatim in clips you do not change; never create new t-refs.)
    - Every clip starts and ends on a phrase or scene boundary; never cut inside a phrase; a cut on a scene boundary that falls inside a word will be moved to the word edge by the harness (<=0.4 s) or rejected.
    - Output ids: filename-safe ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$, unique, short (reel_1, reel_2, wide_1).
    - Produce exactly the number of outputs requested; fill `brief` with how you read the instruction (outputs_requested, target_duration_s, aspect, captions_language, style_words) — the harness checks the plan against your own brief.
    - Duration: sum of (end-start)/speed per output within ±10% of target_duration (hard limit ±25%); when the instruction gives no duration use the preset's default and say so in reasoning.
    - speed: 1.0 for clips that contain speech; 1.25–2.0 allowed only for speech-free clips when pace is dynamic; crop 'auto_face' for 9:16 talking-head clips, 'center' otherwise.
    - captions: enabled when the instruction asks for subtitles; language = the requested one (e.g. 'uz' even if speech is 'ru' — translation happens later); style = preset.caption_style. titles: at most 2 per output, `at` in output-timeline seconds, text <= 40 chars in the captions language (or the instruction's language). music per preset/instruction.
    - Do not reuse the same phrase in two outputs unless the instruction asks for variants; keep narrative order within an output unless 'dynamic' asks for a hook first.
 5. Editing heuristics by pace. dynamic: open with the strongest highlight (hook) in the first 3 s, clips 2–6 s, alternate scenes when possible, end on a complete phrase; calm: clips 5–15 s, follow the original order; always prefer complete highlight phrases over partial scenes; for 9:16 prefer phrases from scenes with people_count>=1 when the pack knows it; mixed-language videos: prefer phrases in the requested caption language unless the instruction says otherwise.
 6. Tool policy (the fewest-calls justification). "Tools are optional. Your final answer is validated automatically and any problems are sent back to you, so do NOT call validate_edl just to check a normal plan. Call get_transcript_range / get_scene_details only in COMPACT mode or for word-level timing around a scene edge. Call preview_frame only when the instruction depends on what is visible and the descriptions cannot answer it; ask for every frame you need in one turn (several preview_frame calls at once), budget 6 per job. Call validate_edl before answering only for unusual plans (>3 outputs, >15 clips, deliberate scene/phrase boundary mixing, after frames changed the plan)."
 7. Output contract. "Answer with the plan JSON only (the output format is enforced). reasoning: 2–6 sentences in the instruction's language explaining the hook, the structure and any trade-off (e.g. duration). No seconds anywhere except titles.at."
 8. Repair protocol. "If you receive VALIDATION ISSUES, return the complete corrected plan: fix every error, keep everything else identical (same output ids, same refs), do not add commentary."

Task text (buildTaskText): 'INSTRUCTION:\n<user prompt verbatim>\n\nPRESET: <name>\nMODE: FULL|COMPACT\nTOOLS: available|not available (answer directly)\nProduce the plan now.'
Repair text (buildRepairText): 'VALIDATION ISSUES (attempt k of 2):\n' + formatIssuesForModel(errors) + optional warnings + '\nReturn the complete corrected plan.'
Revise text (buildReviseText): 'CURRENT PLAN (ids; t-refs are hand-set times, keep them unless you change that clip):\n<JSON draft>\n\nEDIT REQUEST:\n<edit>\n\nReturn the complete updated plan. Outputs you do not touch must be byte-identical (same ids, refs, captions, titles). Change only what the request requires.'

Pack content order (renderPack, deterministic): media -> preset -> phrases (sorted by start; id p<index>) -> scenes (sorted by start; id s<index>; phrases = ids overlapping >50 ms) -> highlights (as sorted in highlights.json, cap 40; phrases = ids overlapping) -> mode. Numbers round2; no file paths; no frame paths (preview_frame is the only frame access). Size for a 10-min video: ~200 phrases x ~45 tokens + 60 scenes x ~40 tokens + 40 highlights x ~30 tokens ≈ 13–15k tokens, far below the 40k compact threshold; FULL mode is the norm for the SPEC range.
design.loop_and_validation:
runPlannerLoop(backend, ctx, task, opts):
  limits: maxRepairs=2, maxCalls=12 (API requests incl. tool round-trips), per-turn max_iterations=8 (backend), frameBudget=6, maxToolCalls=12 (enforced inside tool run(): over budget => is_error result, loop continues), maxTokens 16000 -> 32000 once on max_tokens.
  0. If ctx.phrases.length===0 && ctx.sceneRefs.length===0 => PlanError('nothing_to_plan') before any call (no cost).
  1. taskText = task.kind==='plan' ? buildTaskText(...) : buildReviseText(draftFromEdl(task.currentEdl, ctx), task.edit).
  2. turn = await backend.start({ system: SYSTEM_PROMPT, packText: ctx.packText, taskText, tools: opts.tools ?? [], outputSchema: PlanDraftSchema, maxTokens }). calls += turn.calls; onTurn(turn).
  3. Classify turn.stopReason: 'refusal' => fail('refusal', category) (no repair — a refused structured output is not schema-valid); 'max_tokens' (after the backend's own one bump) => fail('max_tokens'); 'max_iterations' => fail('loop', 'tool loop did not converge'); 'error' => fail.
  4. Parse: draft = PlanDraftSchema.safeParse(JSON.parse(turn.text)) — try JSON.parse first; on SyntaxError the API backend also tries betaZodOutputFormat(PlanDraftSchema).parse(text) for its terser error; the agent backend may return a fenced block, so strip ```json fences before parsing. Failure => issues=[{error,'invalid_json'|'schema', message}] and go to repair (step 6) — these count as repairs.
  5. resolved = resolveDraft(draft, ctx, { mode: task.kind, currentEdl }). Checks per output, in this order, each producing PlanIssue {severity, code, output, clip?, message, suggestion?}:
     - bad_id (regex) / duplicate_id / no_outputs / no_clips: error.
     - per clip: parseRef null => unknown_ref error listing 3 nearest valid ids by time if the index is numeric ('p212 does not exist; last phrase is p187'); raw t-ref in plan mode => raw_time error unless within 30 ms of a boundary (then snapped, warning) — in revise mode a t-ref is accepted when the clip equals a clip of currentEdl (carried over); end<=start => empty_clip error (message shows resolved seconds); start<0 or end>duration => out_of_media (clamp if <=0.5 s overflow with warning, else error); speed outside [0.25,4] => bad_speed error; speed!=1 while the clip overlaps a phrase => speech_speed warning.
     - word safety: snapClipsToWords(resolvedClips, ctx.transcript, 0.4) — snapped edges => warning cuts_word with the note text; edges that could not be snapped (shift >0.4 s) => cuts_word error with suggestion 'use pN.start / sM.end instead'.
     - overlap between clips of one output => warning; the same clip range in two outputs => warning (only informs).
     - duration: target = output.target_duration ?? brief.target_duration_s; if set: |expected-target| > max(0.25*target, 5 s) => duration_off error (message gives expected, target, and the 3 phrases adjacent to the output's last clip with their durations as add/remove candidates); > max(0.10*target, 2 s) => warning.
     - count: brief.outputs_requested set and != outputs.length => count_mismatch error.
     - captions.enabled && !language => captions_no_language warning, fill from brief.captions_language ?? majority phrase lang; style defaults to preset.caption_style. titles: at > expected duration => title_outside warning and clamp to expected-1; text > 60 chars => warning.
     - Build z.input<OutputSchema> for outputs with zero errors; EdlSchema.safeParse of {outputs: valid, reasoning} as a final guard (its issues become 'schema' errors on the offending output).
  6. If resolved.errors === 0 => status 'ok', return (edl from resolved). Else if repairs < maxRepairs && calls < maxCalls: repairs++; fixed.push(...errors); turn = await backend.continue(turn, buildRepairText(errorsAndWarnings, repairs, maxRepairs)); goto 3. Else: outputs with no errors become the EDL => status 'partial' (issues of the dropped outputs kept in report.issues); zero valid outputs => status 'failed' with error 'план не прошёл проверку после 2 исправлений: <first error>'.
  7. Returned LoopResult carries all turns (usage/usd summed), toolCalls (from tools' onCall), fixed (errors that triggered repairs), issues (remaining), draft (last parsed draft, or null).
plan(jobId, opts) wraps it: load media.json (required; else PlanError), transcript.json/scenes.json/highlights.json optional (missing => empty, warning), preset via loadPreset; ctx = buildPlanContext; tools = opts.tools===false ? [] : makePlannerTools(ctx, { frameBudget, onCall, extractFrame: toolDeps?.extractFrame }); backend = opts.backendInstance ?? selectBackend(...). onTurn logs cost immediately (see cost field). After the loop (also in catch/finally): write plan.json (PlanReportSchema) always; on ok/partial write edl.json via writeJson(EdlSchema) and return { ...report, edl, partial: status==='partial' } so runStep records 'ok'/'partial'; on failed write edl.draft.json (raw draft, if any) and throw PlanError (runStep records 'failed' with the message; the CLI prints it and the hint; the process exits non-zero only for the run/plan command, the job stays usable). 'Step failures must not crash the pipeline' is thus satisfied the same way ingest/understand do it: state in job.json, artifacts on disk, cost logged, retry via `vedit plan <id> -p ...` or manual `vedit cut <id> --edl`.
Call accounting (fewest calls): happy path 1 call (~30–60 s at medium effort); frames requested in one turn 2 calls; one repair 2 calls; worst case bounded by maxCalls=12 (≈ 3 turns x up to 4 tool round-trips) — realistically ≤4.
Revise (src/plan/revise.ts): load edl.json (required), same ctx (same pack bytes => cache hit if within TTL), task {kind:'revise', edit, currentEdl}; loop as above (resolve in revise mode accepts carried-over t-refs); on ok/partial: copy edl.json to edl.v<N>.json (N = count of existing versions + 1), write new edl.json, diff = diffEdl(prev, next), affected = added + changed, write revise.json (ReviseReportSchema incl. diff and affected), log cost with step 'revise'; the CLI then runs cut(jobId, edl, media, { only: affected, transcript, snap }) — removed outputs' rough_<id>.mp4 are left in place (listed in the report). Known limitation to fix alongside: cut() rewrites cut.json whole, so a `--only` re-cut loses the records of untouched outputs — change cut() to merge by id before stage 5 ships.
design.cost_and_caching:
Pricing (src/plan/pricing.ts), USD per MTok for claude-opus-5-5 from the bundled docs (PRICES_AS_OF 2026-10-06; confirm against the live pricing page before relying on ceilings): input 4, output 20 (thinking tokens are already inside output_tokens), cache read 0.2, cache write 5 (5 m) / 8 (1 h), batch 2/10. usdForUsage(model, u): if u.iterations?.length => sum per entry priced by entry.model (handles server-side fallbacks); else w5 = u.cache_creation?.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens ?? (u.cache_creation_input_tokens ?? 0), w1 = u.cache_creation?.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens ?? 0, usd = (input_tokens*in + w5*cacheWrite5m + w1*cacheWrite1h + (cache_read_input_tokens ?? 0)*cacheRead + output_tokens*out)/1e6; service_tier==='batch' => batch rates. Unknown model => {usd:0, priced:false} and a report warning 'цена модели X неизвестна, usd=0' (never throws). input_tokens is the UNCACHED remainder; cache fields are never double-counted.
Logging (cost.json via existing addCost, one entry per API request so a crash mid-loop loses nothing): plan.onTurn => for each request inside the turn (the API backend returns per-message usage in Turn.handle.perCall) addCost(jobId, { step: 'plan' | 'revise', provider: 'anthropic' | 'claude-agent-sdk' | 'mock', model, units: { input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, calls: 1, tool_calls: n, images: k }, usd }). Agent backend: a single entry per query() with usd = total_cost_usd and units from modelUsage (estimate; plan.json.priced=false, CLI prints '≈'). Mock: usd 0 like local compute. plan.json repeats the totals (usage, usd, calls) and `vedit status` prints 'план: 2 вызова, $0.19 (api, claude-opus-5-5, medium)'.
Expected cost per job (10-min video, FULL mode, pack ≈ 15k tokens incl. system+tools): first call writes the cache 15k x $5/M = $0.075 and emits ~3–5k output tokens incl. thinking x $20/M = $0.06–0.10 => ≈ $0.15–0.18; a repair or frame round-trip re-reads 15k x $0.2/M = $0.003 + new tail ~2–5k input + ~3k output ≈ $0.08; typical job $0.15–0.30; revise within the TTL ≈ $0.08–0.12, after the TTL + $0.06 for a cold pack. Agent backend: similar tokens, but the figure is the SDK's estimate.
Caching rules the implementation must keep (and a live test checks): tools array name-sorted and the same instances for all calls of a job; SYSTEM_PROMPT a constant with no interpolation; pack rendered from objects built in fixed key order with round2 numbers (no Date.now(), job id, paths, pid); effort/model fixed per conversation; repair and revise append — never edit or delete earlier messages (also required by Opus 5.5 preserved-thinking binding); never change tool_choice (default auto everywhere). cacheTtl '5m' default; '1h' (ttl:'1h' on the system and pack blocks, top-level automatic breakpoint stays 5 m — longer-TTL entries precede shorter ones as the docs require) for sessions where a revise within the hour is likely (CLI --cache-ttl 1h). Minimum cacheable prefix on Opus 5.5 is 512 tokens — system+tools alone (~2.5k) clear it. Health signature per the notes: call 2+ of a job must show cache_read_input_tokens >= pack size; cache_read 0 means a silent invalidator — tests/live-plan.ts asserts it and plan.json stores per-call usage so it is visible after the fact.

 3. resolveDraft: GOOD_DRAFT => 0 errors, EdlSchema.parse succeeds with defaults filled; unknown ref => unknown_ref error naming the last valid id; end<=start => empty_clip; outputs_requested 3 vs 1 output => count_mismatch; target 30 with 12 s of clips => duration_off error with candidate phrases in the message; scene edge inside a word => cuts_word WARNING and the resolved src_start === 8.29 (snapped via snapClipsToWords); a 1.2 s shift => cuts_word ERROR; bad id 'reel 1' => bad_id; duplicate ids; titles.at beyond duration => clamped + warning; revise mode accepts a carried-over t-ref and rejects a new one.
 4. tools (makePlannerTools with extractFrame: async () => Buffer.from(TINY_JPEG_BASE64,'base64')): sorted names; get_transcript_range returns overlapping phrases with words and errors on a 200 s range; get_scene_details returns edges.inside_word for s1; preview_frame returns one image + text, 7th call returns isError with the budget message, out-of-range t errors; validate_edl output equals resolveDraft on the same draft; onCall receives a record per call.
 5. loop with MockBackend: (a) happy path — one turn with GOOD_DRAFT => status ok, calls 1, repairs 0, mock.received is empty; (b) repair — turn 1 BAD_DRAFT_UNKNOWN_REF, turn 2 GOOD_DRAFT => ok, calls 2, repairs 1, fixed contains unknown_ref, mock.received[0] contains 'unknown_ref' and 'p99'; (c) exhausted — three bad turns => status failed with error, draft non-null, issues non-empty; (d) partial — 2 outputs, one unfixable after 2 repairs => status partial, edl has 1 output; (e) tool execution — a turn with tools:[{name:'validate_edl', input:{plan: BAD}}, {name:'preview_frame', input:{t:5}}] then GOOD_DRAFT => toolCalls.length 2, the validate result text lists the error, image budget decremented; (f) stopReason 'refusal' => failed with code refusal and no repair; (g) invalid JSON text => counted as a repair with code invalid_json; (h) maxCalls reached => failed code loop; (i) usage/usd summed across turns.
 6. plan() end to end with backendInstance: MockBackend against a temp job dir seeded with media.json/transcript.json/scenes.json/highlights.json/job.json/cost.json (written with writeJson + the real schemas) => edl.json valid, plan.json valid (PlanReportSchema), cost.json has one entry per turn with provider 'mock', usd 0; failing run => edl.draft.json present, plan.json status failed, cost still logged, PlanError thrown; tools:false => backend receives tools [].
 7. revise(): seeded edl.json with 2 outputs; mock returns a draft that changes reel_1's clips and keeps wide_1 byte-identical => diff {changed:[{id:'reel_1', fields:['clips']}], unchanged:['wide_1']}, affected ['reel_1'], edl.v1.json exists, revise.json valid; diffEdl unit cases (added/removed/changed captions).
 8. pricing: usdForUsage('claude-opus-5-5', {input 1000, output 500, cache_read 15000, cache_creation 0}) === (1000*4 + 500*20 + 15000*0.2)/1e6 within 1e-9; 1h split via cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens; iterations[] with a fallback model entry priced by that model; unknown model => {usd 0, priced false}; service_tier 'batch'.
 9. backend selection: selectBackend('auto', ..., {ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:'x'}) => api; without key and with the CLI binary resolvable => agent with the policy note; 'mock' without instance => throws.
 10. prompt stability: SYSTEM_PROMPT contains no '${', no digits that look like dates, and buildTaskText output differs only in the instruction between two calls.
Backend-specific code (anthropic.ts, agent.ts) is covered by: a type-level test (tsc) and tests/live-plan.ts (manual, needs credentials; asserts the first live request with tools + output_config.format is accepted, the repair/second call shows cache_read_input_tokens > 0, and plan.json usage matches the summed per-call usage). npm run typecheck must pass for src/ (the pre-existing red in tests/make-fixtures.ts — undefined SpeechPart, duplicate 'parts' — should be fixed in the same stage so CI is green).

Shared planner options (added to run, plan, revise; parsed by plannerOpts()): --backend <auto|api|agent> (default auto), --model <id> (default claude-opus-5-5), --effort <low|medium|high|xhigh|max> (default medium), --max-repairs <n> (default 2), --no-tools ('без инструментов: один вызов со структурированным ответом'), --frames <n> (бюджет кадров preview_frame, default 6), --cache-ttl <5m|1h> (default 5m).

vedit run <video> -p/--prompt <text> [--preset bold_pop] [-e/--edl <file>] [--skip-understand] [--no-snap] [--language] [--vision] [+ planner options]
  - After ingest/understand: if --edl => existing stageEdl path (bypasses the agent entirely). Else if no --prompt => keep today's message but reworded: 'нет инструкции: передайте --prompt "..." или готовый план --edl <file>' and return (exit 0, job reusable). Else: console.log('▸ plan'); const r = await runStep(job.id, 'plan', () => plan(job.id, { instruction: opts.prompt, preset: opts.preset, ...plannerOpts(opts) })); printPlan(r); then the existing cut step with r.edl (skip cut when r.edl is null — cannot happen on ok/partial).
  - printPlan(r): '  backend: api, claude-opus-5-5, effort medium' (+ backend note when agent), per output '  ✔ reel_1 9:16 29.4s/30s 5 клипов, субтитры uz' (✖ with the first error for dropped outputs in partial), '    ⚠ ' per warning (cuts_word snaps, duration warnings, preset fallback), tool calls summary '  инструменты: preview_frame x2, validate_edl x1' when any, cost line '  стоимость: $0.1872 (2 вызова, 1 исправление, кэш 15.2k)' with '≈' for unpriced (agent) usage, reasoning (first 300 chars) on its own line.
  - Failure: runStep marks 'plan' failed; the catch prints '✖ plan: <message>' plus 'черновик: workspace/<id>/edl.draft.json — исправьте и запустите vedit cut <id> --edl <file>, или повторите: vedit plan <id> -p "..."' and exits 1 (same convention as other steps).

vedit plan <job_id> -p/--prompt <text> [--preset <name>] [--cut] [+ planner options]
  - Standalone planning for an existing job (requires media.json; warns if transcript/scenes missing). Stores the prompt/preset into job.json (updateStep is not enough — extend writeJson of job with prompt/preset or add a small saveJobMeta()). Runs runStep(jobId,'plan',...) and printPlan; with --cut continues into cut (transcript loaded via loadTranscript, snap on). Hint printed at the end: 'нарезать: vedit cut <id>'.

vedit revise <job_id> -p/--prompt <text> [--no-cut] [--no-snap] [+ planner options]
  - Replaces the stage-5 stub now (design reused as-is): runStep(jobId,'revise', () => revise(jobId, { edit: opts.prompt, ...plannerOpts(opts) })); prints the diff ('  изменено: reel_1 (clips, titles); без изменений: wide_1; удалено: —; добавлено: reel_3'), cost line, then unless --no-cut: runStep(jobId,'cut', () => cut(jobId, edl, media, { only: affected, transcript, snap })) and printCutReport. Requires edl.json (error 'сначала vedit plan <id> -p ...').

vedit status <job_id>: after the understand line, if plan.json exists print 'план: <status>, <calls> вызов(а), <repairs> исправл., $<usd> (<backend>, <model>, <effort>)' and the first 3 warnings; if revise.json exists print the last diff summary. The existing 'стоимость API' line already reflects cost.json totals.

Also: bump program.version to match package.json (0.3.0 for stage 3), update README status table (stage 3 ✔, stage 5 revise ✔ planner-side, render pending), .env.example gets VEDIT_PLANNER (auto|api|agent) and a comment that ANTHROPIC_API_KEY selects the api backend and that the agent backend uses the Claude Code login.
risks: VERIFY LIVE (highest priority): the bundled docs list structured outputs as compatible with batches/streaming/token counting/thinking but say nothing about combining output_config.format with client tools in one request, nor whether the final end_turn text after tool turns is schema-constrained. Mitigation built in: tools are optional, the first request feature-detects (on BadRequestError retry once without tools, warning recorded), --no-tools gives a guaranteed single-call path, and format.parse failures fall into the repair loop. tests/live-plan.ts checks this on the first run with credentials.

VERIFY LIVE: whether non-required (zod .optional()) properties are accepted in output_config.format schemas; fallback is .nullable() (anyOf with null is listed as supported) at the cost of the model emitting explicit nulls.

VERIFY LIVE: betaZodTool sends zod 4's raw JSON schema (`$schema`, and `minimum`/`maxLength` if constraints were used). The design deletes `$schema` defensively, uses no numeric/string constraints in tool shapes, and does not set strict:true (the research notes flag strict + raw zod keys as unverified).

Subscription login through the Agent SDK is undocumented for third-party products (docs: third parties may not offer claude.ai login; personal non-distributed scripts are not addressed) — this is not legal advice; the user must confirm against Anthropic's Commercial Terms. The api backend with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is the supported SPEC path; the agent backend is an explicit, clearly labeled fallback whose cost figures are client-side estimates (plan.json.priced=false). Also unverified: that `resume: sessionId` re-attaches the MCP server + outputFormat for the repair call (fallback: stateless repair), that MCP ImageContent from preview_frame is forwarded to the model as an image, and that a Cyrillic cwd (C:\Users\firda\монтаж) works for the spawned CLI on Windows (set cwd to the job dir, which is ASCII-safe only if VEDIT_WORKSPACE is; consider CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME if transcript paths are an issue).

Model errors the validator cannot catch: a wrong but self-consistent brief (e.g. it reads '3 рилса' as 2 and makes 2 outputs) passes count_mismatch; a hook choice that is editorially poor passes everything. Accept for MVP; the eval loop (contact sheet + manual review) is the guard. Consider a cheap deterministic parse of 'N рилс/ролик/видео' and 'NN сек' in the instruction as a second opinion later.

Scene boundaries from ffmpeg often fall inside words; auto-snap (<=0.4 s) keeps SPEC's no-cut-words rule but can shorten/extend a clip slightly versus the model's intent; shifts >0.4 s become repair errors. Highlights from the stub are heuristic (loudness/length), so 'dynamic' plans may lean on them — stated in the prompt.

max_tokens truncation for very large plans (many outputs x many clips): a 16000 cap includes thinking; the backend bumps once to 32000 (explicit client timeout avoids the SDK's non-streaming guard). If plans ever exceed that, switch the backend to stream:true + finalMessage() (notes cover the pattern) and set eager_input_streaming on tools.

Cache economics: 5-minute TTL means a revise after the user has watched the output usually pays the pack again (~$0.06 for 15k tokens) — acceptable; --cache-ttl 1h is available. Any accidental non-determinism in renderPack (object key order, float formatting) silently kills caching — the unit test on byte-identity and the live cache_read assertion exist for this reason.

Opus 5.5 specifics (from the notes): forced tool_choice is a 400 (design never forces); thinking cannot be disabled (effort pinned to medium); preserved-thinking binding means the transcript must stay append-only (continue() only appends; max_tokens retry rebuilds from the pre-truncation prefix without replaying the cut-off assistant message — verify this is accepted; otherwise start a fresh conversation for the retry).

Cost logging granularity vs the existing cost.json convention: one entry per API request adds a few entries per job; `vedit status` shows the total only. Prices are hard-coded from docs dated 2026-10-06 — add a PRICES_AS_OF warning in `status` when older than 90 days, or fetch live pricing in a later stage.

Loop limit edge: when max_iterations is hit while the model still requests tools, the runner returns a tool_use message without executing tools; the design fails the plan ('loop') rather than appending a user message after a dangling tool_use (which would 400). Tool-level budgets (6 frames, 12 tool calls => is_error results) make this rare. Optional refinement (verify the exact setMessagesParams signature in BetaToolRunner.d.ts:20-61): take over the turn by appending synthetic is_error tool_results plus 'answer now'.

Revise correctness depends on cut.json keeping records of outputs not re-cut; cut() currently rewrites cut.json whole on --only runs (noted in research). Fix cut() to merge by id before stage 5 ships, and keep removed outputs' rough files (reported, not deleted).

Compact mode (packs > ~40k tokens, i.e. videos far beyond the 10-minute SPEC target) is designed but not exercised by any real fixture; the token estimate is a chars/2.8 heuristic. Validate with countTokens (client.beta.messages.countTokens) in tests/live-plan.ts before relying on the threshold.
npm run typecheck is currently red because of tests/make-fixtures.ts (pre-existing); fix it in this stage so the new backend code's type checks are trustworthy.
The @modelcontextprotocol/sdk peer dependency of the Agent SDK must be installed for createSdkMcpServer (check node_modules; the lockfile already pins the win32-x64 CLI binary).

design.title: Stage 3 design — Hybrid planner with budget, provider abstraction and revise-ready harness
design.summary: One conversation harness (class Planner in src/plan/planner.ts) serves both stage 3 plan() and stage 5 revise(). It holds the job context (media, transcript, scenes, highlights, preset), a frozen system prompt, a deterministic cached context block, five tools defined once with zod (get_transcript_range, get_scene_details, preview_frame, validate_edl, submit_edl) and a Budget (USD, API iterations, repair turns, tool calls, preview frames, wall clock). The model never returns the EDL as free text by contract: it must call submit_edl, which runs the same validateEdl() that validate_edl runs (zod EdlSchema + media clamp + word/phrase/scene boundary rule with auto-snap <= 0.4 s + duration tolerance). The harness has three acceptance paths in order: submit_edl -> JSON found in the final text -> a repair turn (max 2) -> last valid candidate from validate_edl history (marked partial). A PlannerBackend interface has three implementations: AnthropicBackend (client.beta.messages.toolRunner + betaZodTool, prompt caching, per-iteration usage -> USD via a pricing table), AgentSdkBackend (query() + createSdkMcpServer/tool(), runs on the Claude Code subscription login, cost from result.total_cost_usd/modelUsage as an estimate) and MockBackend (scripted turns for tests + a deterministic highlight heuristic for `--planner mock`). Auto selection: API key -> anthropic; else login credential present -> agent-sdk (today's effective default on this machine); else a clear PlannerError. revise(instruction, currentEdl) reuses the same prefix, tools and validation, then diffEdl(prev, next) computes per-output added/removed/changed/unchanged and the exact `rerender` set that the CLI passes to cut(..., { only }). Every conversation writes one cost.json entry (step 'plan' or 'revise') even on failure, plus plan.json / revise.json trace files. Offline tests run on MockBackend with no network, ffmpeg or whisper.
design.backend_choice:
PROVIDER ABSTRACTION (src/plan/backend/types.ts)

interface PlannerBackend {
  readonly name: 'anthropic' | 'agent-sdk' | 'mock';
  readonly model: string;          // e.g. 'claude-opus-5-5'
  readonly note: string;           // one line shown by the CLI, e.g. 'agent-sdk — вход Claude Code (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY не задан)'
  run(input: BackendTurnInput, tools: PlannerToolDef[], opts: BackendRunOptions): Promise<BackendResult>;
}
interface BackendTurnInput { system: string; contextBlock: string; task: string; prior?: BackendTranscript /* opaque, for repair */; repairText?: string }
interface BackendRunOptions { budget: BudgetTracker; effort: 'low'|'medium'|'high'; maxTokens: number; signal: AbortSignal; onEvent: (e: PlannerEvent) => void }
interface BackendResult { finalText: string; stopReason: 'end_turn'|'max_tokens'|'refusal'|'max_iterations'|'budget'|'aborted'|'error'; stopDetails?: string; requests: number; usage: UsageTotals; usd: number; usdIsEstimate: boolean; transcript?: BackendTranscript }
type UsageTotals = { input_tokens; output_tokens; cache_read_input_tokens; cache_creation_input_tokens; thinking_tokens } (all numbers, 0 when unknown)

Tools are defined ONCE as PlannerToolDef<I extends z.ZodObject> = { name; description; inputSchema: I; run(input: z.infer<I>, ctx: ToolCtx): Promise<ToolResult> } with ToolResult = { text: string; images?: { base64: string; mediaType: 'image/jpeg' }[]; isError?: boolean }. Each backend adapts them:
- anthropic: `{ ...betaZodTool({ name, description, inputSchema, run: async (args, c) => wrap(def, args, c?.signal) }) }` from '@anthropic-ai/sdk/helpers/beta/zod'. wrap() counts the call against the budget, converts ToolResult to `string | BetaToolResultContentBlockParam[]` (image -> { type:'image', source:{ type:'base64', media_type:'image/jpeg', data } }) and throws `new ToolError(text)` (from '@anthropic-ai/sdk/lib/tools/ToolError') for isError so the tool_result carries is_error:true. Do NOT set strict:true (research unknown: zod 4 raw schema carries $schema/minimum/maximum/pattern which the docs list as unsupported in strict mode). Tools are sorted by name and the array is built once per Planner instance (cache stability).
- agent-sdk: `tool(def.name, def.description, def.inputSchema.shape, async (args) => ({ content:[{type:'text',text}], isError }))` — tool() takes the raw zod shape, hence `.shape` of the ZodObject; all five go into `createSdkMcpServer({ name:'vedit', version:'1.0.0', tools })`. Image blocks in MCP results are NOT covered by the research notes -> verify; until verified preview_frame in this backend returns text '[кадр сохранён в <path>; просмотр изображения недоступен в этом бэкенде]' and the prompt tells the model to rely on scene descriptions.
- mock: calls def.run directly.

SELECTION (src/plan/backend/index.ts): `selectPlannerBackend(choice: PlannerChoice = (process.env.VEDIT_PLANNER as PlannerChoice) ?? 'auto', opts: { model?: string }): Promise<{ backend: PlannerBackend; note: string }>` with PlannerChoice = 'auto'|'anthropic'|'agent-sdk'|'mock'.
auto rules, in order:
 1. process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set -> AnthropicBackend (note 'anthropic — API key').
 2. else process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set OR exists(path.join(process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? path.join(os.homedir(), '.claude'), '.credentials.json')) -> AgentSdkBackend (note 'agent-sdk — вход Claude Code по подписке; стоимость в cost.json — оценка SDK, не счёт'). The harness only checks the file exists; it never reads it.
 3. else throw PlannerError('no_backend', 'нет ANTHROPIC_API_KEY и нет входа Claude Code (claude /login или CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN). Варианты: задать ключ в .env; выполнить `claude /login`; или `--planner mock` — эвристический план без LLM (помечен [mock])').
Mock is never chosen automatically (same honesty convention as the stub vision provider: the user asks for it explicitly).
CONCRETE DEFAULT TODAY: on this machine ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are unset and ~/.claude/.credentials.json exists, so `vedit run --prompt ...` resolves to agent-sdk. Policy caveat (must be stated in README and in the CLI note): the Agent SDK docs say third-party developers may not offer claude.ai login for their products; personal, non-distributed use of one's own Pro/Max login is not addressed. Treat it as undocumented, keep `anthropic` the recommended production path, and let a key flip the default automatically.

AnthropicBackend (src/plan/backend/anthropic.ts): `new Anthropic({ maxRetries: 3, timeout: 300_000 })` (the runner's request options cannot carry timeout/maxRetries). Default model 'claude-opus-5-5' (override: opts.model / VEDIT_PLANNER_MODEL / --model). Params per run (object literal, `stream: false as const` to get BetaToolRunner<false>):
  { model, max_tokens: 16000 (<= 21333 non-streaming SDK guard), max_iterations: budget.remainingIterations(), thinking: { type:'adaptive' }, output_config: { effort }, betas: ['server-side-fallback-2026-07-01'], fallbacks: 'default', cache_control: { type:'ephemeral' }, system: [{ type:'text', text: SYSTEM_PROMPT, cache_control:{ type:'ephemeral' } }], tools: sortedTools, messages }.
  No tool_choice (forced tool_choice is a 400 on Opus 5.5), no temperature/top_p/top_k, no prefill, messages end with a user turn.
AgentSdkBackend (src/plan/backend/agent-sdk.ts): `query({ prompt: contextBlock + '\n\n' + task (+ repair text), options: { systemPrompt: SYSTEM_PROMPT, mcpServers: { vedit: server }, tools: [], allowedTools: ['mcp__vedit__*'], permissionMode: 'dontAsk', settingSources: [], model, maxTurns: budget.maxIterations, maxBudgetUsd: budget.maxUsd, cwd: os.tmpdir(), env: { ...process.env, CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME: 'vedit' } } })`. Spread process.env (options.env replaces, not merges; USERPROFILE must survive so the CLI finds the login). Read the 'system' init message to assert the tools array contains only mcp__vedit__* (log a warning otherwise). Effort/thinking option names for query() are not in the research notes -> verify before wiring --effort to this backend (ignore the flag with a printed note until verified). Repair turns here are a fresh query() whose prompt appends 'Предыдущая попытка не вызвала submit_edl; последние ошибки валидации: ...' (no transcript continuation API in the notes).
MockBackend (src/plan/backend/mock.ts): see offline_testing.

tools.output: JSON text: { phrases: [{ i: number, start: number, end: number, lang: string, text: string, words?: [[w, start, end], ...] }], gaps: [[start, end], ...] (silences >= 0.3 s between phrases inside the range), truncated: boolean }. Phrases overlapping [start,end]; numbers rounded to 2 decimals.
tools.why: The cached context block carries phrases without words to stay small for 10-minute videos; the model fetches word timestamps only for candidate ranges, which is what it needs to place edges on phrase/word boundaries.

tools.name: get_scene_details
tools.input: { index?: number (scene index), start?: number, end?: number } — at least one of index or start/end (checked in run(), isError otherwise). zod: z.object({ index: z.number().optional().describe('scene index from the context'), start: z.number().optional(), end: z.number().optional() })
tools.output: JSON text: { scenes: [{ i, start, end, description, objects: string[], people_count, emotion, shot_type, quality_score, frame: 'frames/shot_00i.jpg' | null, phrases: number[] (indices of phrases overlapping the scene) }] }. `frame` is set only when <dir>/frames/shot_<i padded 3>.jpg exists (stub emits one scene per shot, so i == shot index; not guaranteed by schema, hence the exists() check). Descriptions starting with '[stub]' are passed through unchanged so the model sees they carry no visual information.
tools.why: Scene text in the context block is truncated to 80 chars; this returns the full record and the phrase mapping needed to align cuts with scene boundaries.

tools.name: preview_frame
tools.input: { t: number (seconds) } — zod: z.object({ t: z.number().describe('timestamp in seconds; use sparingly, each call costs image tokens') }). run(): clamps t to [0, media.duration-0.05]; counts against budget.maxPreviewFrames (6) — when exhausted returns isError 'preview budget exhausted; rely on scene descriptions and transcript'.
tools.output: ToolResult { text: 'frame at 12.400s (scene 1, phrase 3: "...")', images: [{ base64, mediaType: 'image/jpeg' }] }. File written to <dir>/frames/preview_<ms>.jpg via opts.frameExtractor (default extractFrame(media.normalized_path, t, file, 640) from src/understand/shots.ts). Anthropic backend sends it as an image content block in the tool_result; agent-sdk backend sends the text only until MCP image results are verified; mock returns the ToolResult as is.
tools.why: SPEC §5.3 requires it; it is the only way the model can check framing (speaker in frame for 9:16) because the stub vision provider invents nothing. Capped because each 640px JPEG costs roughly 0.5-1k input tokens per later turn.

tools.name: validate_edl
tools.input: { edl: EdlDraft } where EdlDraft = { outputs: [{ id: string, aspect: '9:16'|'1:1'|'16:9', target_duration?: number, clips: [{ src_start: number, src_end: number, speed?: number, crop?: 'center'|'auto_face' }], captions?: { enabled: boolean, language?: string, style?: string }, titles?: [{ at: number, duration?: number, text: string, style?: string }], music?: { enabled: boolean } }], reasoning?: string } — zod EdlDraftSchema (plain objects, no refine/regex/default so z.toJSONSchema is trivially representable).
tools.output: JSON text ValidationReport: { ok: boolean, errors: string[], warnings: string[], boundaries: [{ output, clip, edge, t, kind: 'word'|'phrase', word?, suggested, shift }], stats: [{ id, clips, duration, target? }], snapped_edl?: EdlDraft (present when the only problems were word-edge shifts <= 0.4 s; already applied) }. Never isError for validation failures (the model must read them); isError only for non-object input. Side effect: if ok, state.lastValid = report.edl (best candidate for budget exhaustion).
tools.why: Dry run of exactly the same validateEdl() that submit_edl uses, so the model can iterate before committing; its history also provides the 'last valid candidate' fallback.

tools.name: submit_edl
tools.output: JSON text: { accepted: true, edl: Edl (defaults filled, snaps applied), warnings: string[] } or { accepted: false, errors: string[], boundaries: [...] }. On accepted: state.submitted = edl; a second accepted submit replaces the first (last submit wins) and adds a warning to the trace. Not isError on rejection.
tools.why: Opus 5.5 does not allow forced tool_choice and the toolRunner does not auto-parse output_config.format, so an explicit commit tool is the deterministic way to get a validated EDL out of the conversation; it is the 5th tool beyond SPEC's four and is documented as 'validate_edl + commit'.

design.prompt_outline:
Render order and caching (Anthropic backend): tools (sorted by name, fixed for the Planner instance) -> system[0] (frozen SYSTEM_PROMPT, cache_control ephemeral) -> messages[0].content[0] = context block (cache_control ephemeral, byte-stable) -> messages[0].content[1] = task text (no marker) -> top-level cache_control ephemeral walks the growing tool_use/tool_result tail. That is 3 of 4 breakpoints. Revise starts a NEW conversation with the identical tools+system+context prefix (cache hit if within 5 min; otherwise a cheap re-write) and a different task text. Old message history is never replayed (avoids thinking-block signature binding issues and keeps plan/revise symmetric across backends).

SYSTEM_PROMPT (English, ~800 tokens, answers in the user's language), sections in order:
1. Role: 'You are the planning agent of an automated short-form video editor. You turn one source video plus its analysis into an EDL (edit decision list) that ffmpeg will cut exactly as written.'
2. Inputs you will receive in the first user message: a JSON context block (media, phrase-level transcript with per-phrase language, scenes, highlights ranked by a measurable-signal heuristic, style preset) followed by the task. Everything else is fetched with tools.
3. Hard rules (numbered): (a) every clip edge must lie on a phrase boundary, in a silence gap between phrases, or on a scene boundary; never inside a word; (b) 0 <= src_start < src_end <= media.duration; clip length between preset.pacing.min_clip_seconds and max_clip_seconds unless the instruction says otherwise; (c) output ids are filename-safe ([a-zA-Z0-9_-]) and unique: reel_1, reel_2, wide_1...; (d) aspect: 'рилс/reels/shorts/tiktok/сторис' -> 9:16, 'youtube/широкий' -> 16:9, default 9:16; (e) total duration per output within ±10% of target_duration (compute Σ(src_end-src_start)/speed); (f) captions.language is the language the USER asked subtitles in (e.g. 'субтитры на узбекском' -> 'uz') even when speech is another language; captions.style = preset.captions.style; (g) titles: <= preset.titles.max_words words, only facts present in the transcript, no invented claims; (h) crop 'auto_face' for 9:16 when a person speaks on camera, else 'center'; (i) reasoning: 2-5 sentences in the user's language, naming which phrases/highlights were chosen and why.
4. Honesty: scene descriptions prefixed '[stub]' contain no visual observation — do not describe visuals you have not seen; use preview_frame (limited budget) if framing matters; if the budget is exhausted, say so in reasoning.
5. Workflow (prescriptive, with trigger conditions): read the context; shortlist candidate ranges from highlights and phrases; CALL get_transcript_range with include_words=true for each candidate range before choosing exact timestamps; CALL get_scene_details when a cut might cross a scene change; CALL preview_frame at most a few times for framing checks; CALL validate_edl, fix every error, then CALL submit_edl exactly once; after acceptance reply with at most three sentences and stop. Do not paste the EDL as text; do not ask the user questions; if the instruction is ambiguous choose the most common interpretation and state it in reasoning.
6. Budget note: 'You have a limited number of tool calls and preview frames; tool errors starting with "budget" mean you must submit now with the best valid plan.'
7. Revision mode (one short paragraph, always present so the system prompt stays frozen): 'When the task says REVISION, change only what the edit request requires, keep untouched outputs identical, keep ids stable, omit outputs the user asks to remove, and explain the delta in reasoning.'

Context block (buildContextBlock, deterministic): {'media': {duration, width, height, fps}, 'transcript': {'language', 'phrases': [[i, start, end, lang, text], ...]}, 'scenes': [[i, start, end, shot_type, quality_score, description<=80 chars], ...], 'highlights': [[start, end, score, reason<=80 chars], ... top 40], 'preset': Preset}. Numbers rounded to 2 decimals; arrays of arrays with a one-line legend prefixed as text; no words, no timestamps of generation. For a 10-minute video (~150 phrases, ~100 shots, 40 highlights) this is roughly 8-12k tokens; for the 35 s example it is < 512 tokens, so that breakpoint silently does not cache (fine).

Plan task text (buildPlanTask): 'TASK: plan\nINSTRUCTION: <user text verbatim>\nPRESET: <name>\nReply language: same as the instruction.' Revise task text (buildReviseTask): 'TASK: REVISION\nCURRENT EDL (accepted earlier):\n<JSON of current Edl>\nPREVIOUS REASONING: <edl.reasoning>\nEDIT REQUEST: <user text>\nRules: minimal change; unchanged outputs byte-identical; submit the FULL edl via submit_edl.' Repair text (buildRepairText): 'You ended without calling submit_edl. Call submit_edl now with a complete, valid EDL. Last validation errors: <list or "none">.'
design.loop_and_validation:
Planner.converse(kind, task):
1. tracker = new BudgetTracker(budget); state = { submitted: null, lastValid: null, validations: [], previewFrames: 0, toolCalls: 0 }; tools = this.tools (bound to state/tracker); signal = tracker.signal(opts.signal).
2. result = await backend.run({ system, contextBlock, task }, tools, { budget: tracker, effort, maxTokens: 16000, signal, onEvent }).
   AnthropicBackend.run: builds the params literal (see backend_choice) and iterates `for await (const message of runner)`: (a) usage -> normalizeUsage + usdForUsage(message.model ?? model) -> tracker.addRequest(usd); emit {type:'request'}; (b) if message.stop_reason === 'refusal' -> record stop_details.category/explanation, break; (c) if 'max_tokens' -> break (the runner would stop anyway; tools in that message are never executed); (d) if tracker.exceeded() === 'usd' -> break with stopReason 'budget' (the iterator's finally aborts pending tools; do NOT await runner.done() after a break — research unknown says it may hang; use the message in hand). Text blocks of each assistant message are emitted as {type:'text'}; thinking blocks are left untouched (display omitted; `--verbose` sets thinking.display 'summarized' and prints summaries). After the loop: requests = iterations consumed; if the last message still has tool_use and the cap was hit -> stopReason 'max_iterations'. transcript = structuredClone(runner.params.messages) for repair (readonly view of the append-only history; verify it includes the auto-appended assistant/tool_result turns). Typed errors: APIUserAbortError -> 'aborted'; AuthenticationError -> PlannerError('api_error', 'ключ не принят (401)'); RateLimitError/InternalServerError after the SDK's own retries -> PlannerError('api_error'); APIConnectionError checked before APIError.
   AgentSdkBackend.run: iterate query(); 'assistant' messages -> emit text; 'result' success -> finalText = m.result, usd = m.total_cost_usd (usdIsEstimate true), usage from m.modelUsage summed; subtypes error_max_turns -> 'max_iterations', error_max_budget_usd -> 'budget', error_during_execution / is_error -> 'error' with m.errors joined; wrap the loop in try/catch because query() throws after an error result.
   MockBackend.run: executes the script (see offline_testing).
3. Acceptance, in order: (i) state.submitted -> acceptedVia 'submit_edl'. (ii) else extractJson(result.finalText) (first balanced {...} block or ```json fence) -> validateEdl(..) ok -> acceptedVia 'final_text' + warning 'EDL взят из текста, submit_edl не вызван'. (iii) else if repairs < budget.maxRepairs and tracker.exceeded() === null and result.stopReason in ['end_turn','max_iterations'] -> repairs++, emit {type:'repair'}, run again with { prior: result.transcript, repairText: buildRepairText(...) } (Anthropic: new toolRunner with messages = prior + user repair message — same tools/system so preserved thinking signatures stay valid; max_iterations = remaining; agent-sdk: fresh query with the repair text appended to the prompt) and go back to 3. (iv) else if state.lastValid -> acceptedVia 'last_valid', partial = true, warning 'принят последний валидный черновик (бюджет/лимит: <reason>)'. (v) else throw PlannerError: 'refusal' (with stop_details), 'budget_exceeded', 'truncated' (max_tokens), or 'no_edl' (end_turn without any valid draft). The cost entry is written in a finally block before rethrowing so failed attempts are still logged.
4. Return PlanOutcome; plan()/revise() in src/plan/index.ts write files: edl.json (writeJson EdlSchema), plan.json or revise.json (PlanReportSchema/ReviseReportSchema), history/edl_<ISO>.json of the previous EDL on revise; partial = acceptedVia === 'last_valid' || (warnings include a duration-out-of-tolerance warning) — runStep then records 'partial'.

validateEdl(input, { media, transcript, scenes }, { phraseRule = 'error', maxSnap = 0.4, durationTolerance = t => Math.max(2, 0.1 * t) }):
 a. EdlSchema.safeParse(input) -> on failure errors = formatIssues lines; return ok:false (nothing else can run).
 b. Per output: sanitizeClips(clips, media) from src/cut/index.ts -> its warnings are copied (clamped/skipped/auto_face); zero clips left -> error.
 c. Word rule: checkClipBoundaries(clips, transcript); for each issue shift = |suggested - t|; shift <= maxSnap -> apply snapClipsToWords result and warning 'snapped'; shift > maxSnap -> error 'clip k start/end cuts the word "..." — move to X' with BoundaryReport kind 'word'.
 d. Phrase/scene rule on the snapped clips: isOnBoundary(t) false (t strictly inside a phrase beyond tol 0.15 s and not within 0.15 s of a scene edge) -> BoundaryReport kind 'phrase' with suggested = nearestBoundary(t) (phrase start/end, gap, scene edge within 1.5 s) -> error when phraseRule === 'error', warning otherwise.
 e. Duration: expectedDuration(clips) vs target_duration -> warning 'длительность Xs отличается от цели Ys' when |diff| > tolerance (never an error; the prompt asks for ±10%).
 f. Order/overlap: clips sorted by src_start are allowed in any order (montage), but identical clips within one output -> warning; src_start equal to src_end after snapping -> error.
 g. Titles: at within [0, output duration] else warning; text longer than preset max_words -> warning.
 h. ok = errors.length === 0; edl = the parsed EDL with snaps applied; stats per output.
Limits summary: maxIterations 12 API requests per conversation including repairs (runner max_iterations = remaining each time), maxRepairs 2, maxToolCalls 40 (tool wrapper returns isError 'budget: tool call limit reached — call submit_edl now' once exceeded; submit_edl and validate_edl are exempt from the cap so the model can always finish), maxPreviewFrames 6, maxUsd 1.00 (checked between requests; the last request may overshoot by one turn), maxWallMs 240 s via AbortSignal (SPEC §8 wants a 10-min video done in <= 5 min end-to-end). CLI flags map onto these. Step failure never crashes the pipeline: plan() throws PlannerError, runStep records status 'failed' + error in job.json, the CLI prints it with a hint ('vedit plan <id> -p ...' re-runs without re-ingesting; '--planner mock' for an offline plan) and exits 1 with all earlier artifacts intact.
design.cost_and_caching:
Cost per conversation is one cost.json entry via addCost(jobId, { step: 'plan' | 'revise', provider: backend.name, model, units, usd }), written in a finally block (so refusals/budget stops/API errors still log what was spent). units = { requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, thinking_tokens, tool_calls, preview_frames, repairs, wall_seconds, estimate: 0|1, unpriced: 0|1 }. CostEntry has no free-text field, so 'estimate: 1' marks Agent SDK values (client-side estimate from result.total_cost_usd / modelUsage; on a subscription this is not a bill) and 'unpriced: 1' marks a model missing from PRICES (usd logged as 0 rather than crashing). Mock logs usd 0 with model 'mock', matching the local-compute convention.
Anthropic pricing (src/plan/pricing.ts, USD per MTok for claude-opus-5-5 from the bundled docs; confirm against the live pricing page): input 4, output 20 (includes thinking tokens; output_tokens is authoritative), cache read 0.2, cache write 5m 5, cache write 1h 8. usdForUsage: if usage.iterations is a non-empty array, price each entry by its own model (a server-side fallback rescue is billed at the fallback model's rate; a 'fallback_message' entry is counted too), else usd = input_tokens*4e-6 + (cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens ?? cache_creation_input_tokens ?? 0)*5e-6 + (cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens ?? 0)*8e-6 + (cache_read_input_tokens ?? 0)*0.2e-6 + output_tokens*20e-6. input_tokens is the uncached remainder; never add cache fields twice. If usage.service_tier === 'batch' apply 2/10 (not expected here). Totals are summed per iteration by the backend because the runner does not aggregate and done() only returns the final message's usage.
Caching layout and invariants: tools array built once per Planner and sorted by name; SYSTEM_PROMPT is a constant with no dates/ids; context block is produced by buildContextBlock with fixed key order and rounding (a standing test asserts byte equality across two calls); the task text follows the context block in the same user message without a marker; top-level cache_control walks the tail. Effort is pinned per route (plan and revise both default 'medium', set explicitly; changing effort between requests invalidates the messages cache, but plan and revise are separate conversations so only the tools+system prefix needs to match). Minimum cacheable prefix is 512 tokens: the system+tools prefix (~1.8k tokens) always qualifies; the context block qualifies for videos longer than a few minutes. Health check recorded in plan.json: for request n >= 2, cache_read_input_tokens should be > 0; the CLI prints '⚠ кэш промпта не сработал' when every request after the first shows 0 cache reads (signals a silent invalidator). Agent SDK backend: the CLI manages its own caching; we only record what modelUsage reports.
Budget economics for a 10-minute video on Opus 5.5 (estimate, medium effort, ~8 requests, 6-10 tool calls, 2 preview frames): ~12k cached context + ~2k tools/system written once (~$0.07), cache reads ~8×14k×0.2e-6 (~$0.02), uncached tail growth ~20-30k (~$0.10), output incl. thinking ~8-10k (~$0.18) -> about $0.35-0.45; the default maxUsd 1.00 leaves room for two repairs. A 35 s clip is ~$0.10-0.15. Both numbers must be re-checked after the first live run against cost.json.
design.offline_testing:
MockBackend (src/plan/backend/mock.ts) implements PlannerBackend without network, ffmpeg or whisper. Constructor takes either a script MockTurn[] or 'heuristic'. Scripted run(): for each turn, for each call -> finds the PlannerToolDef by name, parses input with def.inputSchema (so test scripts hit the same zod validation as the API path), invokes the same wrapper used by real backends (budget counting, event emission, isError mapping), stores the ToolResult text in the trace; then the turn's text becomes finalText when it is the last turn. If `prior`/`repairText` are passed (a repair round), the script continues from a second array `repairScript` given in the constructor; if none is given it returns an empty end_turn. Synthetic usage per turn (default input 1200 / output 300 / cache_read 0 then 1000) so pricing and cost.json plumbing are exercised; model 'mock' is absent from PRICES so usdForUsage returns unpriced -> usd 0. Heuristic mode: heuristicEdl(ctx, instruction) parses count ('3 рилса', '2 reels'), duration ('по 30 секунд', '30 сек', '1 мин'), aspect keywords, caption language ('на узбекском' -> 'uz', 'на русском' -> 'ru', 'uzbek' -> 'uz'); packs highlights by score into clips bounded by phrase boundaries until the target is reached (never splitting a phrase), one output per requested reel with disjoint clips, reasoning '[mock] эвристика по highlights: ...'; then runs validate_edl and submit_edl through the tools exactly like a model would, so the mock path still covers the acceptance code.
Test plumbing: Planner is constructed directly with an in-memory PlannerContext (tests/helpers/plan-fixtures.ts) and PlannerOptions { backend: new MockBackend(script), costSink: entries.push, frameExtractor: async (t, file) => { await fs.writeFile(file, FAKE_JPEG); return file } } with ctx.dir = a per-test folder under os.tmpdir(); no VEDIT_WORKSPACE juggling is needed for harness tests. One integration test of plan(jobId) uses a temp workspace: because WORKSPACE_ROOT is computed at import time, the test sets process.env.VEDIT_WORKSPACE first and then `await import('../src/plan/index.ts')` dynamically, seeds <ws>/<job>/{job.json, cost.json, media.json, transcript.json, scenes.json, highlights.json} with writeJson, runs plan() with backend 'mock', and asserts edl.json + plan.json exist and cost.json has one 'plan' entry.
tests/stage3.test.ts cases (node:test + assert/strict, top-level test() like stage1/2):
 1. happy path: script [get_transcript_range(8,14,include_words) ; validate_edl(draft with edge inside 'Каждое') ; submit_edl(fixed draft) ; text 'готово'] -> acceptedVia 'submit_edl', edl parsed with defaults, trace.tool_calls length 3, cost entry provider 'mock' usd 0, events contain 3 'tool' entries.
 2. final-text fallback: no submit, finalText contains ```json {...}``` -> acceptedVia 'final_text' with the warning.
 3. repair: first script ends with plain text, repairScript submits -> repairs === 1, acceptedVia 'submit_edl'; with no repairScript and no lastValid -> rejects with PlannerError code 'no_edl' after maxRepairs rounds.
 4. last_valid: validate_edl ok then nothing else and budget maxRepairs 0 -> acceptedVia 'last_valid', partial true.
 5. validateEdl unit: word edge <= 0.4 s is snapped (warning), > 0.4 s is an error; mid-phrase edge -> error with suggested nearest boundary and -> warning when phraseRule 'warn'; edge in a gap passes; edge within 0.15 s of a scene boundary passes even mid-phrase; src_end > duration clamped with warning; duplicate ids and bad id regex -> schema errors; duration off by > max(2 s, 10%) -> warning only.
 6. tool input validation: get_transcript_range with end <= start -> zod error surfaces as isError result and the loop continues; range > 180 s -> isError 'range too wide'.
 7. budget: maxToolCalls 2 -> third get_transcript_range returns isError starting with 'budget', submit_edl still allowed; maxPreviewFrames 1 -> second preview_frame isError; maxUsd 0.0001 with usagePerTurn priced via a test PRICES override of model 'mock' -> stopReason 'budget' and lastValid used.
 8. pricing: usdForUsage('claude-opus-5-5', usage with cache fields) equals the hand-computed number; iterations[] with a fallback model entry is priced per entry; unknown model -> { usd: 0, unpriced: true }.
 9. context determinism: buildContextBlock(ctx) === buildContextBlock(structuredClone(ctx)) and does not contain 'preview' timestamps or words; for longContext(1500) the block length is < 60k characters (sanity for 10-minute videos).
 10. diffEdl: changed clips in reel_1, captions-only change in reel_2, removed wide_1, added reel_3 -> rerender ['reel_1','reel_3'] for cut (needsCut) while stages.reel_2 === ['design','render']; identical EDLs -> all unchanged, rerender [].
 11. heuristic mock: heuristicEdl(cafeContext(), '2 рилса по 10 секунд, субтитры на узбекском') -> 2 outputs 9:16, captions.language 'uz', every edge on a phrase boundary, durations within tolerance, reasoning starts with '[mock]'.
 12. agent-sdk adapter shape: toMcpTool(def) is built with def.inputSchema.shape and returns { content:[{type:'text'}], isError:true } for a ToolResult with isError (pure function, no query()).
Live tests are not part of `npm test`; a separate `npx tsx tests/live-plan.ts <job_id>` script (skipped without credentials) runs the real backend twice and asserts cache_read_input_tokens > 0 on the second run.
design.cli:
Shared options added to run / plan / revise: `--planner <auto|anthropic|agent-sdk|mock>` (default 'auto', env VEDIT_PLANNER), `--model <id>` (default 'claude-opus-5-5', env VEDIT_PLANNER_MODEL), `--effort <low|medium|high>` (default 'medium'), `--budget <usd>` (default 1.00), `--max-iterations <n>` (12), `--loose-boundaries` (phraseRule 'warn'), `--verbose` (print tool call lines and thinking summaries when the backend supports display 'summarized').
vedit run <video> -p/--prompt <text> [--preset bold_pop] [--edl file] ...: after ingest and understand: if --edl -> stageEdl as today (bypasses the agent entirely); else if --prompt -> `console.log('▸ plan')`, `const r = await runStep(job.id, 'plan', () => plan(job.id, { instruction: opts.prompt, backend: opts.planner, model, effort, budget: { maxUsd: opts.budget, maxIterations }, preset: opts.preset, phraseRule, onEvent: printPlannerEvent }))` then printPlan(r) and continue to '▸ cut' with the returned edl (cut(job.id, r.edl, media, { transcript, snap: opts.snap })); else (no prompt, no edl) keep the current hint text but reword: 'нет --prompt и нет --edl: план не построен. vedit plan <id> -p "..." построит edl.json по анализу'. --skip-understand with --prompt -> fail early with 'планировщику нужны transcript.json/scenes.json; уберите --skip-understand'. The run description becomes 'полный пайплайн: ingest → understand → plan → cut'.
vedit plan <job_id> -p/--prompt <text> [--preset] [planner options] [--cut]: loadJob; requires media.json + transcript.json + scenes.json + highlights.json (PlannerError 'missing_inputs' otherwise with hint 'vedit understand <id>'); runStep('plan', ...) ; prints; with --cut also runs cut for all outputs; otherwise prints 'нарезать: vedit cut <id>'. Re-running overwrites edl.json and plan.json and appends a new cost entry (the previous edl.json is copied to history/edl_<ISO>.json first).
vedit revise <job_id> -p/--prompt <text> [planner options] [--no-cut]: loadJob; current = readJson(edl.json) (fail 'нет edl.json — сначала vedit plan'); `const r = await runStep(jobId, 'revise', () => revise(jobId, { instruction, current, ... }))`; prints the diff: '  ~ reel_1: clips' / '  + reel_3' / '  - wide_1' / '  = reel_2 (без изменений)'; then unless --no-cut and if needsCut(r.diff).length > 0: '▸ cut (только reel_1, reel_3)' -> runStep('cut', () => cut(jobId, r.edl, media, { only: needsCut(r.diff), transcript, snap })) ; removed outputs: delete rough_<id>.mp4 is NOT done automatically (print 'удалить вручную: rough_wide_1.mp4'). Because cut.json is rewritten whole by a --only run, the CLI (or a small change in cut()) must merge the new report into the existing cut.json by output id before writing — call this out in the implementation PR (research unknown #9).
Console conventions (match cli.ts): first line 'job <id>'; '▸ plan' header; '  бэкенд: <backend.note>, модель <model>, effort <effort>'; with --verbose per tool call '  ⚙ get_transcript_range 8.0–14.0s (+слова) 12ms' / '  ⚙ preview_frame 12.4s' / '  ⚙ validate_edl → 2 ошибки' / '  ⚙ submit_edl → принято'; result lines '  ✔ reel_1: 9:16, 3 клипа, 29.4s (цель 30s), субтитры uz' per output and '  ✖' never (a plan either exists or the step failed); '    ⚠ <warning>' four-space warnings; summary '  запросов 7, инструментов 9, повторов 0, $0.31 (anthropic)' or '... ~$0.31 (оценка, agent-sdk)'; final 'готово за X.Xs — workspace/<id>/'. Errors go through fail(): '✖ plan: <message>' plus a one-line hint keyed by PlannerError.code (no_backend -> the three options; refusal -> 'модель отказалась: <category>'; budget_exceeded -> 'поднимите --budget или упростите инструкцию'; no_edl -> 'повторите с --effort high или --planner mock').

scores.critique: Closest to SPEC §4/§5.3/§9 in spirit: a real tool-use agent with the four SPEC tools plus a strict submit_edl, phrase/scene boundary rule (E_BOUNDARY ±0.15 s, silence-gap tolerance as warning, strictBoundaries switch), word-cut rule reusing validate.ts, auto-repair ≤0.4 s on submit, atomic writes, plan.json always written, cost in finally, honest '[fallback]' EDL only behind --allow-fallback. SDK usage is accurate: I verified in BetaToolRunner.js that the public generateToolResponse() runs the current message's tools and caches them so the runner does not re-run them, and that overriding input_schema with a sanitized schema on the spread betaZodTool object is legal. The sanitizer + one-shot non-strict retry is the best answer to the unverified strict/$schema unknown. Weaknesses: (1) cost/latency — DEFAULT_LIMITS allow 24 API iterations, 60 tool calls, 12 frames and $3; its own estimate ($0.7–0.9/10-min video, ~15 Opus 5.5 turns with thinking) is 2–4x the other designs and there is no wall-clock budget at all, so §8's ≤5-minute guideline is at risk; (2) the strict-retry triggers on BadRequestError whose message 'mentions strict/input_schema' — string-matching contradicts the notes' 'never string-match error messages'; (3) no partial result without --allow-fallback: a run that produced a validate_edl-clean draft but never got submit accepted still fails the step (C's last_valid path is kinder and equally safe); (4) `--skip-understand --prompt` is said to fall back to 'scene boundaries only', but scenes.json is also produced by understand, so boundaryCandidates collapse to {0, duration}; (5) max_iterations: remaining must never reach 0 (0 = unlimited per notes) — nextAction ordering happens to prevent it, but it is implicit. Testability is excellent (pure nextAction policy shared with the mock, schema snapshot test, correct dynamic-import handling of WORKSPACE_ROOT).

The ref grammar (clips as phrase/scene ids, harness resolves to seconds) is the strongest possible guarantee of the §5.3 boundary rule and makes revise elegant (draftFromEdl with t-refs for hand edits, outputs byte-identical unless touched). Cheapest by far (1–2 calls, ~$0.2) and its Agent SDK claims go beyond the notes and are correct — I verified effort/thinking/outputFormat/resume/structured_output/error_max_structured_output_retries in sdk.d.ts and that the explicit client timeout disables the SDK's non-streaming max_tokens guard (messages.js:39-43). But the architecture hinges on one unverified API combination (output_config.format + client tools in one request on Opus 5.5) and the designed fallbacks degrade away from the SPEC: feature-detect drops the tools entirely, --no-tools is a non-SPEC path, and the system prompt actively discourages validate_edl/get_* — §5.3/§9 say 'Claude с tool use' and list the four tools as the agent's instruments, so conformance is by the letter, not the spirit. Robustness gaps: no USD cap on the API backend (only iterations), 'never break' means a runaway tool loop runs to max_iterations×repairs, `resume` re-attaching the MCP server + outputFormat is unverified (stateless fallback noted), and the rigid id grammar cannot express a cut at a word boundary inside a long whisper segment, which will bite 'dynamic 2–6 s clips' on talky footage. Factual slips: VEDIT_WORKSPACE 'set per test' does not work because WORKSPACE_ROOT is computed at import (A and C handle this with dynamic import); PRICES for claude-opus-5/claude-opus-4-8 and PRICES_AS_OF are not in the research notes (unsourced). Good: count_mismatch against the model's own brief, nothing_to_plan guard before spending, one cost entry per request so a crash loses nothing, edl.draft.json on failure, partial = valid outputs kept.

Best balance for a skeptical §8 reading: five tools (SPEC four + submit_edl), isOnBoundary/nearestBoundary implementing 'phrase or scene boundary' with gap tolerance and a --loose-boundaries escape, word rule via existing validate.ts, and a BudgetTracker covering USD, iterations, repairs, tool calls, frames AND wall clock (240 s via AbortSignal — the only design that maps §8's ≤5-minute guideline to a hard limit). Failure handling is the most honest: three validated acceptance paths (submit_edl → JSON in final text → last valid validate_edl candidate marked partial), repair turns, exactly one cost.json entry per conversation written in finally (even on refusal/budget/API error), typed PlannerError codes with per-code CLI hints, mock never auto-selected and prefixed '[mock]' (matches the stub convention), and a cache-health warning in plan.json. Revise is the most complete: diffEdl + FIELD_STAGES maps changed fields to cut/design/render so a captions-only edit skips cut (exactly §5.7's 'only affected outputs'), history/edl_<ISO>.json, revise.json, and the cut.json --only overwrite called out. SDK claims check out (betaZodTool spread, ToolError, tool() with .shape, BetaToolRunnerRequestOptions cannot carry timeout, runner.params.messages is the append-only history, never await done() after break). Weaknesses: no max_tokens retry (fails 'truncated' where A/B retry once); server-side fallbacks enabled by default, so a rescued turn silently runs on another model without Opus 5.5 thinking — should be opt-in like A/B; agent-sdk preview_frame is text-only (conservative but weaker than A/B); image token estimate (0.5–1k per 640px frame) is ~2–3x too high; effort limited to low|medium|high; max_iterations: remaining must be guarded against 0 (= unlimited). Cost (~8 requests, $0.35–0.45, $1 cap) sits between A and B.

factual_errors_found: All three designs inherit an inaccurate research-note claim: 'when max_iterations is hit the last message's tools are not executed and no tool_result is appended'. In the installed 0.133.0 BetaToolRunner.js (iterator at ~103-157) the cap check sits at the TOP of the while loop, after the previous iteration has already appended the assistant message, run its tools via #generateToolResponse and pushed the tool_result user message. So the final allowed iteration's tools DO run (and cost), and the history ends with a tool_result, not a dangling tool_use. context-first's risk note ('appending a user message after a dangling tool_use would 400') and tools-first's '(last message may still carry tool_use)' rest on the wrong premise; failing/stopping there is still safe, but budget accounting must count that last tool round, and a continuation after the cap is actually possible.
